So I do not think you will believe anything but that it is among the fabrications of non-Arabs and the inventions of deceivers who do not distinguish between noble speech and what is base, for the feeble-minded; so it found currency with those whom fondness for narration distracts from what understanding (dirāya) requires. «ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا بعد إذ هديتنا وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة انك أنت الوهاب».»

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الدَّوَابُّ): the plural of دابّة, with the bāʾ doubled, because it is derived from الدبيب (creeping). As for whoever read it with the bāʾ lightened, he dropped it out of dislike of the doubling. الدابّة is the feminine of الدابّ: whatever creeps (دبّ) of animals, that is, walks, like the snake, or on hands and feet, like the infant. الدابّة came predominantly to mean what is ridden and loaded; it applies to the male and the female, and the tāʾ in it is for unity. The diminutive of الدابّة is دويّبة. الدبّاب is one who creeps much, and the weak one who creeps in walking. The poet said:
زعمتني شيخا ولست بشيخ ... إنما الشيخ من يدبّ دبيبا
(You claimed I was an old man, but I am no old man; the old man is only one who creeps along.)
الدبّابة is the feminine of الدبّاب; it was the name of a device that in the past was used in sieges: they would go inside it, then it was pushed to the foot of the fortress and they would breach it while inside it. Then in the modern age it was applied to an armoured vehicle that attacks the enemy's ranks and from which shells are fired (the tank).
(الْحَمِيمُ): water that has reached the utmost heat. استحمّ الرجل: he washed; and استحمّ: he entered the bath (الحمّام). بضّ حميمه: his sweat oozed. It is said to one who has bathed: طابت حمّتك وحميمك (may your bath and your sweat be good); sweat is only good on the healthy and bad on the afflicted, so its meaning is "may Allah make your body healthy", and it is of the category of kināya (metonymy). He heated the water in the محمّ, which is the kettle or the cauldron [Translator's note: the printed text reads الرجل; المرجل (cauldron) seems intended]. "The likeness of the scholar is like the likeness of the حمّة", which is the hot spring. ذابوا ذوب الحمّ: "they melted as the حمّ melts", which is what remains of the fat-tail after its grease has been melted. حُمّ الرجل: he was struck with a severe fever (حمّى), and he is محموم (feverish). He is حميمي and she is حميمتي, that is, my close friend (m./f.); and they are أحمّائي (my intimates). A woman says: هم أحمائي وليسوا بأحمّائي (they are my in-laws, but not my intimates). The common people (العامة) and the الحامّة, that is, the elite, knew that. He is مولاي الأحمّ, that is, the most particular and dearest. The poet said:
وكفيت مولاي الأحم جريرتي ... وحبست سائمتي على ذي الخلّة
(I spared my closest kinsman (the burden of) my offence, and I kept my grazing herd for the one in need.)
حُمّ الأمر: the matter was decreed; حُمّ حمامه: his death was decreed, and the decreed fate (القدر المحموم) and the inevitable decree descended on him.
(يُصْهَرُ): is melted. One says صهرت الشحم, of the pattern قطع, when you melted it; الصهارة is the melted fat-tail; صهرته الشمس: the sun melted it. In the hadith: "The boiling water will be poured from above their heads, and it penetrates the skull of one of them until it reaches his belly, and strips away what is in his belly until it comes out of his feet; that is الصهر; then he is restored as he was."
(مَقامِعُ): the plural of مقمعة, with kasra on the mīm, because it is the instrument of suppression (القمع). One says قمعه يقمعه, of the pattern قطع, when he struck him with something to restrain him and humble him. الميقعة [Translator's note: as printed; المقمعة seems intended] is the hammer; it is also said: the whip. In al-Asās: "قمع خصمه: he subdued and humbled his adversary, so he was subdued (فانقمع) and was humbled (تقمّع); people at the judge's door are متقمّعون (abased). انقمع في بيته and تقمّع: he sat alone. I struck him with the مقمع and the مقمعة and with the مقامع, which is the club. تقمّعت الدواب: the animals drove away from their heads the قمع, which are large blue flies among the flies of pasture that buzz; the singular is قمعة. Al-Jāḥiẓ recited:
كأنّ مشافر النجدات منها ... إذا ما مسّها قمع الذباب
بأيدي مأتم متساعدات ... نعال السبت أو عذب الثياب
(As though the lips of the sweating ones among them, when the gadflies touch them, were — in the hands of a gathering of mourning women helping one another — tanned-leather sandals or the fringes of garments.)
From النجد: sweat. And Aws said:
ألم تر أن الله أرسل مزنة ... وعفر الظّباء في الكناس تقمّع
(Have you not seen that Allah sent a rain-cloud, while the dust-coloured gazelles in their lairs were shaking off the flies?)
And they crown the large bowls with the قمع, plural of قمعة, which is the top of the hump. And of the figurative: "Woe to the funnels of speech (أقماع القول)", who are those who hear but do not retain. So-and-so is a قمع of news: he follows it up and talks about it. And you say: "You have no ears; they are only funnels (أقماع)." In al-Qāmūs and its commentary: "And القمع also, with any of the three vowels on the qāf, is a device placed over a vessel through which liquids are poured into it (a funnel); its plural is أقماع."
The qāf together with the mīm has a wondrous property: when the two come together as the first and second radicals of a word, they indicate subjugation, humiliation and overpowering. You say: قمؤ الرجل قماءة and قمأ قمأ when he became abject and small in people's eyes, and he is abased, قميء; أقمأ الرجل: he humbled him. قمحت السويق and other things, with kasra on the mīm, and اقتمحته, when you took it in your palm to your mouth; from it is القمح (wheat), the grain that is ground and from which bread is made. The months of قماح are the coldest months of winter. Al-Hudhalī said:
فتى ما ابن الأغر إذا شتونا ... وحبّ الزاد في شهري قماح
(What a young man is Ibn al-Agharr when we pass the winter, and provisions are loved in the two months of Qimāḥ!)
And of the figurative: أقمح المغلول, so he is مقمح, when the bar of the shackle that pricks his chin does not let him lower his head: «فهم مقمحون». قمر الرجل: he overcame him and took his property (in gambling). قمر الرجل, with kasra on the mīm: his sight was dazzled by snow; it is as though the moon (القمر) was so called because it is bewildered in its sky. قمز الشيء: he gathered it and took it with his fingertips. قمسه في الماء: he immersed it in the water. He drowned in the قاموس of the sea: in its farthest depth. The dictionary (القاموس) was likened to the depths of the seas because it contains many of the words of the language; it is the name of al-Fīrūzābādī's book on lexicon, and in our time it is applied to every book of lexicon, so it is synonymous with the word معجم; and that is not far-fetched. قمص يقمص, with kasra and ḍamma on the mīm in the imperfect, قماصا, with kasra, like النفار and الشراد (shying and bolting). The boys تقامص (leapt about), and there is مقامصة between them. قمص الفرس: the horse raised its forelegs together, threw them down together and kicked with its hind legs. تقمّص, the reflexive of قمّص: he put on the shirt (القميص); and figuratively it is said تقمّص الولاية والإمارة (he donned the governorship and the command); and the soul تقمّصت: it moved from one body to another body, according to the claim of some. From it is القميص, which is what is worn. قمط الأسير: he tied the captive's hands and feet together with the rope, which is the قماط. قمط الصبي بقماطه: he swaddled the infant in his swaddling, which is the cloth that is wrapped around him in the cradle; the common people use it a great deal, and it is pure, eloquent Arabic. القمّاط is the thief. قمط الطائر أنثاه, and the man his wife: he mated with her. قمقم ما على المائدة: he went after what was on the table and gathered it. قمل رأسه: his head became lice-ridden, and he delouses it. قمّ الشيء يقمّه, with ḍamma on the qāf: he uprooted it; and قمّمه: he dried it. القمن, with two fatḥas, is one worthy of a matter, as though he overpowers it and controls it; it comes in a single form for masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural. It is said: هذا المنزل لك موطن قمن, that is, worthy of your dwelling in it. قمه البعير يقمه قموها: the camel raised its head and did not drink the water, as though something overpowered it. And this is very strange indeed.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past meaning) and jussivisation; تر is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "you". Seeing here is cognitive (ʿilmiyya), because seeing the prostration of these things comes about only through the intellect, not through sight. أنّ and what is in its scope take the place of the two objects of تر; أنّ with its noun, and the clause يسجد is its khabar (predicate); له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسجد; من is the fāʿil (agent); في السموات and من في الأرض [Translator's note: as written] are attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. الشمس and what follows it are a particular (item) conjoined to His saying من في السموات ومن في الأرض. These things were specifically named because it has been reported that some people used to worship them. The prostration includes the angels, humans, mountains, trees, beasts and others; and the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees and beasts were singled out for mention because of their prominence and because prostration seems unlikely from them.
(وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذابُ): this verse has greatly occupied the commentators and grammarians. Whoever forbids using a homonymous word (mushtarak) in both its literal and figurative meanings did not arrange كثير in the series of coordinated single words coming under the governance of the verb, and made it nominative by an implied verb indicated by His saying يسجد, that is: and many of the people prostrate to Him a prostration of obedience and worship. That is because the prostration attributed to non-rational beings is other than the prostration attributed to rational beings, so for them it is not permissible to conjoin it to what precedes, because the verb attributed to the two differs in meaning: the prostration of rational beings is the specific, known manner, and the prostration of non-rational beings is submission and obedience. As for those who permitted using the homonymous word in both its literal and figurative meanings, they coordinate it with what precedes, and they have three interpretations in justification of that:
a- That what is meant by prostration is the general meaning shared between rational beings and others, which is humility and submission, so the commonality is semantic.
b- That verbal homonymy is not prohibited, and the figurative and the literal may share (a word).
c- That it is permissible to combine the figurative and the literal. Further exposition of this topic will come in the Rhetoric section.
A group of the grammarians took a third position: they did not make it nominative by an implied verb, because omission of the verb of an agent is not admissible for them, nor did they coordinate it with what precedes; rather they parsed it as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "obedient", or "requited", or "rewarded", or the like. من الناس is a naʿt (adjective) of كثير, and وكثير حق عليه العذاب is conjoined to the preceding.
(وَمَنْ يُهِنِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرِمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ ما يَشاءُ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; من is conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يهن; الله is the agent; ما is negating; له is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and مكرم is genitive (majrūr) by من in form, a mubtadaʾ nominative in position. إنّ with its noun, and the clause يفعل is its khabar; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).
(هذانِ خَصْمانِ اخْتَصَمُوا فِي رَبِّهِمْ): the sentence is resumptive, set out to narrate the story of those who fought in single combat on the day of Badr, namely Ḥamza, ʿAlī and ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith, and ʿUtba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabīʿa, and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba. It is also said they are the disputants among the People of the Book and the Muslims regarding the religion of Allah. هذان is a mubtadaʾ and خصمان its khabar; the clause اختصموا is a naʿt of خصمان. You may make the clause the khabar and خصمان a badal (substitute) of هذان. في ربهم is attached to اختصموا, and it is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is, concerning His religion. He said خصمان and then put the verb in the plural because الخصم is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and so it is usually kept singular and masculine, and it may be put in the dual and the plural; or the plural is in regard to the meaning, because the disputants were various parties and many groups.
(فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيابٌ مِنْ نارٍ يُصَبُّ مِنْ فَوْقِ رُؤُسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; الذين is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause كفروا is the ṣila; the clause قطعت is the khabar; لهم is attached to قطعت; ثياب is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and من نار is a naʿt of ثياب. A detailed account of the meaning of "garments" here will come in the Rhetoric section. The clause يصب is a second khabar of the relative noun, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لهم, or you make it resumptive. يصب is a passive imperfect verb; من فوق رءوسهم is attached to يصب, and الحميم is the nāʾib fāʿil.
(يُصْهَرُ بِهِ ما فِي بُطُونِهِمْ وَالْجُلُودُ): the clause يصهر is a ḥāl from الحميم, and it is passive; به is attached to it; ما is the nāʾib fāʿil; في بطونهم is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of ما; الجلود is conjoined to ما. Some chose that الجلود be nominative by an implied verb, that is, "and the skins are burnt"; they said: because skins are not melted, but only contract when roasted by fire. So it is of the type: علفتها تبنا وماء باردا ("I fed her straw and cold water"), that is, "and I gave her water to drink", because water is not fodder.
(وَلَهُمْ مَقامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; لهم is a fronted khabar, and مقامع is a postponed mubtadaʾ; من حديد is a naʿt of مقامع. There is a difference about what the pronoun in لهم refers to: it is said it refers to those who disbelieved, and the lām is of entitlement (istiḥqāq); and it is said it refers to the helpers of Hell, that is, the guardians (al-zabāniya), who have not been mentioned before, but the context of the speech indicates them.
(كُلَّما أَرادُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها مِنْ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُوا فِيها وَذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ): كلما is an adverb containing the sense of condition, and it has preceded many times. أرادوا is a verb and agent; أن and what follows it are in the sense of a maṣdar, the mafʿūl bihi of أرادوا; منها is attached to يخرجوا; من غم is a badal of the preceding preposition and genitive noun, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because it (the Fire) includes it (the anguish). It is permissible for من to be causal, so it is also attached to يخرجوا, that is: they want to get out of the Fire because of the anguish that has overtaken them. The clause أعيدوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of كلما; فيها is attached to أعيدوا. The wāw is a conjunction, and the conjoined element is omitted, its implied form being "and it will be said to them"; the clause ذوقوا عذاب الحريق is the speech-object of the omitted verb of saying.

* Rhetoric:
1- Ḥaqīqa (literal usage) and majāz (figurative usage):
Ḥaqīqa is the word indicating its original placement, and majāz is that by which is meant something other than the meaning coined in the origin of the language, as has preceded. We promised you that we would give a satisfying statement about the permissibility of combining the literal and the figurative. The fact is that every majāz has a ḥaqīqa, because it could not validly be called majāz except by its being transferred from a ḥaqīqa coined for it. It is self-evident that all created things need names by which they are indicated, so that each of them is known by its name, for the sake of mutual understanding, which is indispensable. The name coined for the thing named is a ḥaqīqa for it; if it is transferred to something else, it becomes majāz. The fine difference between them is that the ḥaqīqa runs generally across its counterparts. Do you not see that when we say "So-and-so is learned (عالم)", it holds true of everyone possessing knowledge; unlike «واسأل القرية» ("and ask the town"), because that is valid only for some inanimate things and not others, since what is meant is the people of the town, because they are among those whom it is valid to ask. It is not permissible to say "and ask the stone and the dust", though it may be fine to say "and ask the abode and the ruins". Al-Aʿshā said:
ألم تسأل الربع القواء فينطق ... وهل تخبرنك اليوم بيداء سماق
(Have you not asked the deserted abode, that it might speak? And will a far-stretching desert inform you today?)

2- The allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in قطعت لهم ثياب:
In the saying of the Exalted «قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيابٌ مِنْ نارٍ» there is an allegorical metaphor: He made the cutting of the garments and their tailoring to the statures of the unbelievers stand for (the Fire's) encompassing them, along with the sarcasm it contains; that is, it envelops them and contains them as garments envelop and contain their wearer. As for the splendour, it lies in His saying «يُصَبُّ مِنْ فَوْقِ رُؤُسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ», which is what is called irdāf (using a consequent term): for garments cover the whole body except the head, so He singled out the heads for mention by His saying يصب.

dervis-irab:23-25.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): the i'rab of its like has preceded, so refresh your memory of it.
(يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤاً وَلِباسُهُمْ فِيها حَرِيرٌ): يحلون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحلون. من أساور: the statements of the grammarians about it are confused, just as all the grammarians have cited it as evidence for من coming to explain the genus (li-bayān al-jins), namely in His saying من ذهب. Its sign is that it is valid to predicate what follows it of what precedes it, so you say: the bracelets are of gold. Explicative من with its genitive noun is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what precedes it if that is definite, as in the saying of the Exalted «فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثانِ», and in the position of a naʿt (adjective), as in His saying من ذهب. I have not seen among all of them anyone who addressed the i'rab of من أساور except with a vague statement that neither moistens thirst nor quenches it. Perhaps the nearest I see in it is that it is a naʿt of an omitted object, that is: ornaments (حليًّا) originating from bracelets being of gold. Ibn Hishām contented himself with saying it is for commencement (ibtidāʾ); Abū al-Baqāʾ said the like of what we say; al-Zamakhsharī did not address it. Shihāb al-Dīn al-Ḥalabī [Translator's note: printed as الحلي; al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī seems meant] said: "His saying من أساور من ذهب: in the first من there are three aspects: one of them is that it is redundant (zāʾida); the second that it is partitive, that is, some bracelets; and the third that it is to explain the genus. And من in من ذهب is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and it is a naʿt of أساور." His statement is incoherent and self-contradictory, as you see.
ولؤلؤا is conjoined to the position of من أساور, because its position is accusative; so the grammarians said. But al-Zamakhsharī was not satisfied with this view and made it accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "and they are given pearls". The clause يحلون is a ḥāl or a second khabar (predicate) of إنّ. ولباسهم: the wāw is a conjunction; لباسهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), فيها is a ḥāl, and حرير is the khabar.
In this turning from the verbal (sentence) to the nominal there is an indication of permanence, since He did not say "and they wear silk"; it thus indicates that silk is their customary and permanent clothing in Paradise. There is also in it a regard for preserving the verse-endings (fawāṣil), because had He said ويلبسون حريرا, there would have been an alif at the end of the verse-ending in writing and in pausing, unlike the rest.
(وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَهُدُوا إِلى صِراطِ الْحَمِيدِ): the wāw is a conjunction; هدوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; إلى الطيب is attached to هدوا; من القول is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the pronoun latent in الطيب. وهدوا إلى صراط الحميد is conjoined to the previous clause, that is: to the praised path of Allah and His upright religion.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ الَّذِي جَعَلْناهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَواءً الْعاكِفُ فِيهِ وَالْبادِ): إنّ with its noun, and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); the sentence is resumptive. ويصدون: the wāw is a conjunction, and يصدون is conjoined to كفروا. Regarding its conjunction to the past there are interpretations. The first of them is that the imperfect is not intended to indicate a specific time, present or future, but only mere continuity is meant by it; its like is «الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ». Or that it is interpreted as past because it is conjoined to the past; or that it is in its normal sense and the past before it is interpreted as future. Abū al-Baqāʾ and others permitted the wāw to be circumstantial, with the clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of كفروا; and this is an incoherent view, because it is an affirmative imperfect, and such does not take the wāw, and what has occurred of it, rare as it is, is interpreted, so it is not permissible to construe the Quran on it. عن سبيل الله is attached to يصدون; المسجد الحرام is conjoined to سبيل الله; الذي is a second naʿt of المسجد, and the clause جعلناه is the ṣila; نا is the agent and the hāʾ the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); للناس is a ḥāl, because it was a naʿt and was fronted. سواء is the second mafʿūl bihi if جعل takes two objects; if it takes one object, سواء is parsed as a ḥāl from the hāʾ of جعلناه. العاكف is the agent of سواء, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective, so it has the force of a derived active participle, that is, in the sense of مستو (equal), that is: We made it equal therein the one who stays (العاكف), that is, the resident. والباد, with the yāʾ dropped following the script of the Muṣḥaf, is conjoined to العاكف, and its meaning is the one who comes from outside. Ḥafṣ alone read سواء in the accusative; the majority read it nominative, as a fronted khabar, with العاكف والباد a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi or as a ḥāl. The khabar of إنّ is omitted, its implied form being "they have lost" or "they have perished" or the like. Al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as "We shall make them taste of a painful punishment", and he was objected to on the ground that it would then come after المسجد الحرام, and there is in it a separation between the qualifier and the qualified.
(وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussivising conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يرد is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); فيه is attached to يرد. The object of يرد is omitted so as to cover everything it can cover. بإلحاد is a ḥāl, and بظلم is also a ḥāl; they are two synonymous ḥāls, as though He said: whoever intends therein something intended, deviating from the right course, being a wrongdoer. This is preferable to supposing the bāʾ in إلحاد to be redundant and making it the object. Abū ʿUbayda said: "The object of يرد is بإلحاد, and the bāʾ is redundant on the object. Al-Aʿshā said: ضمنت برزق عيالنا أرماحنا (our spears have guaranteed the sustenance of our dependants), that is, رزق." Abū Ḥayyān said: "It is better that يرد be made to contain the sense of يلتبس (to become involved in), so that it takes its object through the bāʾ." نذقه is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the agent is latent, its implied form being "We"; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; من عذاب is attached to نذقه, and أليم is a naʿt. Abū Ḥayyān estimated the khabar (of إنّ) by inferring it from His saying نذقه; and this is an explanatory, not a technical, i'rab, so it is better that it be estimated as an estimation [Translator's note: as written], that is: "We shall make them taste a painful punishment".

dervis-irab:26-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رِجالًا): on foot; the plural of راجل, like قائم and قيام. One says رجل يرجل, with fatḥa on the jīm, رجلا with two fatḥas: he travelled on his feet, not riding. One says: this is a man (رجل), that is, complete among men, of evident manliness (الرّجولية and الرّجولية); this is the manlier (أرجل) of the two men. He is راجل and رجل (on foot), clearly going on foot (الرّجلة); "May Allah carry you (and spare you) from going on foot (عن الرّجلة / من الرّجلة)". A people رجّال, رجال, رجّالة, رجل, رجلى, رجالى and أراجيل (on foot). ترجّلوا في القتال: they dismounted from their mounts in battle for close combat. He saw him and dismounted (ترجّل) for him. A man أرجل: big-footed. A man رجيل and ذو رجلة: a strong walker.
(ضامِرٍ): in al-Mukhtār: ضمر الفرس, of the pattern دخل, and also ضمر with ḍamma, ضمرا on the measure of قفل [Translator's note: printed as فقل], so it is ضامر (lean). A ناقة ضامر and ضامرة (lean she-camel). تضمير الفرس is also that you feed the horse until it grows fat, then reduce it to bare sustenance, and that is in forty days. And البعير is applied to the male camel and the she-camel.
(فَجٍّ): الفج, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, is pluralised as فجاج with kasra on the fāʾ; and الفجاج with ḍamma on the fāʾ [Translator's note: as written]: the wide, clear road between two mountains.
(تَفَثَهُمْ): their dirt; and what is meant by "completing the تفث" is trimming the nails and plucking the armpit. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "تفث تفثا, so he is تفث, like تعب تعبا, so he is تعب, when he has left off oiling and shaving, so that dirt covers him. And the saying of the Exalted «ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ»: it is said it is making lawful what was forbidden to them by iḥrām, after leaving the state of iḥrām." Another said: "التفث: it is said its origin is from التفّ, which is the dirt of the nails, and the fāʾ was changed (to thāʾ), as in معثور for معفور. It is said it is dirt and filth; one says: ما نفثك [Translator's note: as printed; ما تفثك seems intended]? And Quṭrub related: تفث الرجل when his dirt increased on his journey. And the meaning of ليقضوا is: let them do what the one in iḥrām does, of removing hair and dishevelment and the like, when he leaves iḥrām."

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنا لِإِبْراهِيمَ مَكانَ الْبَيْتِ أَنْ لا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئاً): the wāw is resumptive, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, its implied form being "remember"; the clause بوأنا is in a genitive construct with the adverb. بوأنا is a verb and agent; لإبراهيم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بوأنا; مكان البيت is the object of بوأنا. Abū al-Baqāʾ and others chose that the lām be redundant (zāʾida), that is, We lodged him at the place of the House; the evidence for that is the saying of the Exalted «وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ». On the first (view), the meaning of بوأنا is "We prepared". أن is explicative (mufassira), because it occurs after an implied verb of saying, that is, saying to him: do not associate. لا is prohibitive, and تشرك is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا. It is also said that it is maṣdar-forming: We did that so that you would not associate, the prohibition being made its ṣila (relative clause). بي is attached to تشرك, and شيئا is the object of تشرك. The statement of Abū Ḥayyān: "And أن is lightened from the heavy (أنّ) — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this — and the norm is that it be followed by a verb of certainty or of preponderant belief, as is its condition when it is doubled; or it is a particle of explanation — al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this — and its condition is that it be preceded by a clause with the meaning of saying, and بوأنا does not have the meaning of saying. The preferable view in my opinion is that it is the أن that makes the imperfect accusative, since it can be followed by a conjugable verb, past, imperfect and imperative, and the prohibition is like the command."
(وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْقائِمِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ): وطهر: the wāw is a conjunction, and طهر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; بيتي is the object of طهر; للطائفين is attached to طهر; القائمين and الركع are conjoined to what precedes; السجود is a naʿt (adjective) of الركع. It is preferable to make the two words count as a single word, because they are two acts within a single act, which is the prayer.
(وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجالًا وَعَلى كُلِّ ضامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِنْ كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ): أذن is an imperative verb, that is: proclaim the call to the pilgrimage and the command to it. The address is to Ibrāhīm, as the context requires, and all the commentators hold this. From al-Ḥasan (it is reported) that it is an address to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was commanded to do that in the Farewell Pilgrimage; and this is stronger from the standpoint of legislation. في الناس is attached to أذن; بالحج is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, announcing. يأتوك is an imperfect made jussive because it occurs as the answer to the request; the wāw is the agent and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); رجالا is a ḥāl; وعلى كل ضامر is conjoined to رجالا, that is, on foot and riding. يأتين is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and the nūn is the agent; the clause يأتين is a naʿt of كل ضامر, because it has the sense of a plural. It was also read يأتون, as a naʿt of those on foot and those riding. من كل فج is attached to يأتين, and عميق is a naʿt of فج.
(لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنافِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْلُوماتٍ): the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and يشهدوا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after it; it, with its genitive (clause), is attached to يأتوك or to أذّن. منافع is a mafʿūl bihi, and لهم is a naʿt of منافع. يذكروا is conjoined to يشهدوا; the wāw is the agent and اسم الله the mafʿūl bihi; في أيام is attached to يذكروا, and معلومات is a naʿt of أيام. Mention of these days will come in the Benefits section.
(عَلى ما رَزَقَهُمْ مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعامِ فَكُلُوا مِنْها وَأَطْعِمُوا الْبائِسَ الْفَقِيرَ): على ما رزقهم is also attached to يذكروا, and the meaning of على here is causation; its like is the saying of the Exalted «وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلى ما هَداكُمْ», and the saying of the poet:
علام تقول الرمح يثقل عاتقي ... إذا أنا لم أطعن إذا الخيل كرت
(For what reason do you think the spear weighs down my shoulder, if I do not thrust when the horsemen charge?)
من بهيمة الأنعام is attached to رزقهم. فكلوا: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied clause), and كلوا is an imperative verb and agent; منها is attached to كلوا; أطعموا is conjoined to كلوا; البائس is a mafʿūl bihi and الفقير a naʿt.
(ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا بِالْبَيْتِ الْعَتِيقِ): ثم is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command — a useful discussion of it will come in the Benefits section — and يقضوا is an imperfect made jussive by the lām of command; تفثهم is a mafʿūl bihi. وليوفوا نذورهم is conjoined to يقضوا تفثهم, and وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق is also conjoined; بالبيت is attached to يطوفوا, and العتيق is a naʿt of البيت. The secret of its being called "the Ancient" (العتيق) will come in the Benefits section.

* Benefits:
1- The lām of command:
The lām of command, which the grammarians call the lām of request (al-lām al-ṭalabiyya), whether it is a command or a supplication. The first is as in «لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ», and the second as in «لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ». It may also be for entreaty (iltimās). A command is from the higher, a supplication from the lower, and an entreaty from an equal. The lām of command has a kasra, except that when it occurs after the wāw and the fāʾ, it is mostly given a sukūn, as in «فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي»; and it may be given a sukūn after ثم. The lām of command enters the verb of the third person, active and passive, and the second and first persons in the passive.

2- Why the House was called "the Ancient" (العتيق):
The commentators differed about this naming. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that it means the old one, because it is the first House established for mankind. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it was called عتيق because Allah freed it (أعتقه) from the domination of tyrants over it; how many a tyrant marched to it to destroy it, and Allah prevented him. Al-Zamakhsharī said, in support of this aspect: "If you say: al-Ḥajjāj gained power over it and was not prevented? I say: he did not intend to dominate the House; rather Ibn al-Zubayr fortified himself in it, so he devised a stratagem to get him out, then he rebuilt it. And when Abraha intended to dominate it, what was done to him was done," as will come. It is also said: a noble House, from their expression عتاق الخيل والطير (the noble ones among horses and birds).

dervis-irab:54-60.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَيُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (ليعلم) is conjoined to (ليجعل), and what (ليجعل) attaches to has already been given. (الذين) is the fāʿil (agent); the clause (أوتوا العلم) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (العلم) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (أوتوا); (أنه الحق) stands in place of the two objects of (يعلم); (من ربهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads (من ربك)]; (فيؤمنوا) is conjoined to (يعلم), and (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنوا). (فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهادِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) (فتخبت) is conjoined to (فيؤمنوا به); (له) is attached to (تخبت), i.e. their hearts become tranquil towards it; (قلوبهم) is the fāʿil. The wāw is resumptive; (إن) and its noun; (لهاد): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and (هاد) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (الذين) is the object of (هاد), because it is an active participle; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (إلى صراط مستقيم) is attached to (هاد). (وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْهُ) The wāw conjoins to what preceded, in order to complete and exhaust the description of the state of the disbelievers. (لا يزال) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; (الذين كفروا) is its noun and (في مرية) its khabar; (منه) is a naʿt (adjective) of (مرية), which is read with kasra and with ḍamma on the mīm. The pronoun refers to the Qur'an, or to the Messenger, or to what Satan cast. (حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ) (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; (تأتيهم) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after (حتى); the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi and (الساعة) the fāʿil; (بغتة) is a ḥāl; (أو) is a conjunction; (يأتيهم) is conjoined to (تأتيهم); (عذاب يوم) is the fāʿil and (عقيم) a naʿt.
(الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ) (الملك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to one like it, attached to the notion of "being settled" to which the khabar, (لله), is attached; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted [clause], its implied form being "the day they believe" or "the day their doubt ceases" [Translator's note: the text has «حربتهم», evidently a misprint for «مريتهم», "their doubt"]. The clause (يحكم بينهم) is resumptive, as if it came as the answer to an implied question, its implied form being "What will He do with them?", and it was said: He will judge between them. It is not far-fetched that it be a ḥāl of the name of Allah, the adverb being attached to (يحكم). (فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ) The fāʾ conjoins for branching off; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; the clause (وعملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the clause (آمنوا); (في جنات النعيم) is the khabar. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا فَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ) (الذين) is also a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; the clause (كذبوا بآياتنا) is conjoined to the clause (كفروا); (فأولئك): the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ, because of the scent of condition in the relative noun; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ, (لهم) a fronted khabar and (عذاب مهين) a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of (أولئك), and the clause (أولئك …) is the khabar of (الذين).
(وَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ قُتِلُوا أَوْ ماتُوا لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ اللَّهُ رِزْقاً حَسَناً) (وَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ قُتِلُوا أَوْ ماتُوا لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ اللَّهُ رِزْقاً حَسَناً) [Translator's note: the verse heading is repeated in the source.] (قتلوا أو ماتوا) is conjoined to (قتلوا) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably (ماتوا) is conjoined to (قتلوا), and (قتلوا) to (هاجروا)]. (ليرزقنهم): the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (يرزقنهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi and (الله) the fāʿil; (رزقا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (حسنا) a naʿt. The oath clause and its answer are the khabar of (الذين), and this is preferable to positing an implied khabar. (وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير الرازقين) the khabar of (هو), and the clause is the khabar of (إن). (لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ مُدْخَلًا يَرْضَوْنَهُ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ) The lām prepares for the oath; the clause (يدخلنهم) is the answer to the oath, and the oath clause with its answer is a badal (substitute) of the first oath clause, or it is resumptive. The hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; (مدخلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq because it is a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun); the clause (يرضونه) is a naʿt of (مدخلا). (وان الله لعليم حليم): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; (عليم حليم) are khabars of (إن) [Translator's note: the source reads «خبر ان لإن», apparently a slip for «خبران لإن», "two khabars of inna"]. (ذلِكَ وَمَنْ عاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبَ بِهِ) (ذلك) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the iʿrāb of a parallel to it has already been given. The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, or a relative noun, as mubtadaʾ; (عاقب) is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (بمثل) is attached to (عاقب); (ما) is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause (عوقب به) is the ṣila.
(ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنْصُرَنَّهُ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ) (ثم بغي عليه) is conjoined to (عاقب); the lām prepares for the oath, and the oath clause is the khabar of (من); the clause (إن الله لعفو غفور) is causal, with no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
(يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ): an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): a time in which there is no good is likened to barren women; or because on the day of war women's children are killed, so that they become as if barren, never having given birth.

dervis-irab:61-65.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ) The clause is resumptive, establishing His power, Exalted is He, to grant victory: whoever is able to make the night enter the day and the day enter the night, and other marvels of His power, is without doubt able to grant victory. (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the promised victory; (بأن الله) is its khabar (predicate), the bāʾ being causal; the clause (يولج الليل في النهار) is the khabar of (أن); the clause (ويولج النهار في الليل) is conjoined to the first clause; (وأن الله سميع بصير) is also conjoined to (بأن الله …). The meaning of making the night enter the day and vice versa is bringing about the darkness of the one in place of the light of the other, and vice versa. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ) A second resumptive clause, establishing another proof alongside the first proof (which is power over all possibles), namely His being, Exalted is He, the Real, the Established, while everything besides Him is non-existent and passing. (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأن) the khabar; (الله) is the noun of (أن), and the clause (هو الحق), of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is the khabar of (أن). (وَأَنَّ ما يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ هُوَ الْباطِلُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ) Conjoined to what preceded; His saying (من دونه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); (لم) is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; (تر) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (أن) and what falls in its domain stand in place of the two objects of (تر), because it is a verb of knowing, as will come. The clause (أنزل) is the khabar of (أن); (من السماء) is attached to (أنزل) and (ماء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فتصبح): the fāʿ is a conjunction, not causal, because the interrogative is one of affirmation, as we said before, interpreted as a statement, i.e. "you have seen", and a statement has no answer; moreover causality is not sound here, for the seeing does not cause the greening of the earth; rather what necessitates it is the sending down of water after it becomes [green] [Translator's note: so in the source]. More detail on these rhetorical points will come in the Rhetoric section. (فتصبح): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (تصبح) is conjoined to (أنزل); it is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb — the secret of the discrepancy in conjoining an imperfect to a past will come — (الأرض) is the noun of (تصبح) and (مخضرة) its khabar. Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred that (تصبح) be complete (tāmma), (الأرض) its fāʿil and (مخضرة) a ḥāl.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ) The clause gives the reason for what preceded; (إن), its noun and its two khabars.
(لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ) The clause is circumstantial or resumptive. (له) is a fronted khabar and (ما) a delayed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is attached to an omitted [verb that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); (وما في الأرض) is conjoined to (ما في السموات). (وإن الله): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (هو الغني) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is the khabar of (إن); (الحميد) is a second khabar of (هو). (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُمْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالْفُلْكَ تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and the jussive; (تر) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (أن الله) is the object of (تر); the clause (سخر) is the khabar of (أن); (لكم) is attached to (سخر); (ما) is the object of (سخر) and (في الأرض) the ṣila of (ما); (الفلك) is conjoined to (ما), i.e. He subjected to you what is in the earth and subjected to you the ships; the clause (تجري) is a ḥāl of (الفلك); (في البحر) is attached to (تجري) and (بأمره) is a ḥāl. (وَيُمْسِكُ السَّماءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (يمسك) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "He"; (السماء) is the mafʿūl bihi; (أن تقع): the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) — the Basrans assume "out of aversion that it should fall" and the Kufans "lest it fall". Abū al-Baqāʾ and others preferred that it be a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of (السماء), i.e. He holds back its falling, in the sense of preventing it. (على الأرض) is attached to (تقع); (إلا) is a particle of restriction, because the speech is not affirmative, or is equivalent to a negation, i.e. He does not let it fall in any state at all; so it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of states, and His saying (بإذنه) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. bound up with His will, Exalted is He, and His permission; the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa).
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ) The clause is causal; (إن) and its noun; (بالناس) is attached to (رءوف); the shifted lām; (رءوف) is the first khabar and (رحيم) the second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted is He: «أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً», the future imperfect is conjoined to the past, and He did not say (فأصبحت) conjoined to (أنزل); that is to convey the persistence of the rain's effect time after time: the sending down of the water is something whose occurrence has passed, while the greenness of the earth persists and has not passed. This is as when you say: "He bestowed favour on so-and-so, so I go out in the evening and the morning thankful to him"; were you to say "so I went out in the evening and the morning thankful to him", it would not have that effect, because it indicates a past that was and ended. This is a place worthy of reflection.
The question arising here is: why was (فتصبح) not put in the accusative as an answer to the interrogative?
The answer: had it been put in the accusative, it would have given the opposite of what is intended, because its meaning is affirming the greening, and with the accusative it would turn into negating the greening. An example is your saying to your companion:
"Have you not seen that I bestowed favour on you, so you are thankful (فتشكر)?" If you put it in the accusative, you are negating his thankfulness and complaining of his negligence in it; and if you put it in the nominative, you are affirming the thankfulness. Sībawayh said: «I asked him (meaning al-Khalīl) about «أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً», and he said: This is affirmative, and it is a drawing of attention, as though you said: "Do you hear? Allah sent down water from the sky, and such and such happened."» Ibn Kharūf said in his commentary on Sībawayh's Kitāb:
«His saying "he said: this is affirmative" and his saying "and such and such happened" mean that both are past; and he explained the speech with "do you hear" to show you that it is not connected to the interrogative, because the force of the interrogative in it is weak.» One of the commentators on the Kitāb said: «(فتصبح) cannot be put in the accusative because the speech is affirmative; do you not see that the meaning is that Allah sent down the water, and so the earth is in this state?» And al-Farrāʾ said: «He expressed it with the imperfect only because there is in it a depiction of the form the earth is in and the state that has come over the earth, while the past conveys the cessation of the thing. This is like the saying of Jaḥdar ibn Muʿāwiya [Translator's note: the text has «معونة»] al-ʿUklī describing his state in the severest of predicaments, in a story that happened to him with al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf:
يسمو بناظرتين تحسب فيهما ... لما أجالهما شعاع سراج
(He rears up with two eyes in which, when he rolls them, you would think there is the gleam of a lamp.)
لما نزلت بحصن أزبر مهضر ... للقرن أرواح العدا مجاج
(When I came down upon a fortress-like, shaggy, roaring [beast] that spits out the souls of foes at its rival.)
فأكر أحمل وهو يقعي باسته ... فاذا يعود فراجع أدراجي
(So I charge, attacking, while it squats on its haunches; and when it comes back, I go back on my tracks.)
وعلمت اني إن أبيت نزاله ... أني من الحجاج لست بناج
(And I knew that if I refused to fight it, I would not escape from al-Ḥajjāj.)
His saying (فأكر) is a depiction of the state that came over him.
Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī: «It has been said that the fāʾ in this verse is causal, and the causal fāʾ does not necessarily entail immediate succession, as shown by the soundness of your saying "If he becomes Muslim, he enters Paradise", and the interval between the two is known.»
A delightful study by al-Rāzī:
Imām al-Rāzī has a good study here which can be summarised as follows:
«He mentioned here six of the effects of His power:
1- The sending down of water, from which the greening of the earth arises. He explained "seeing" as knowledge rather than sight, because the water, although visible, its being sent down by Allah from the sky is not visible. And He said (فتصبح الأرض) rather than (أصبحت) because it conveys the persistence of the rain's effect time after time.
2- His saying: «له ما في السموات وما في الأرض», among which is the creation of rain and plants as a benefit for living creatures, although Allah has no need of that and does not benefit from it.
3- The subjection of what is in the earth, i.e. He made what is in it tractable for you, such as stone, iron and fire for what is wanted of them, and animals for eating, riding, carrying loads and looking at.
4- The subjection of the ships by means of water and winds; had Allah not subjected them, they would sink or stand still.
5- The holding back of the sky, because the preceding blessings are completed only by it. The sky is a heavy body, and whatever is so must fall unless there is an impediment preventing it, namely the [divine] power; so Allah held it back by His power lest it fall and nullify the blessings by which He has favoured us.
6- Giving life, then death, then life [again]. By this He pointed out that these blessings are for whomever Allah has given life: by the first giving of life He pointed to His favour in this world through all that preceded, and by death and the second giving of life He pointed to His favour upon us in the Hereafter.

dervis-irab:66-70.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَنْسَكاً): with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn, a law (sharīʿa), because it is taken from al-nasīka, which is worship. The discussion of this root has already been given in full.

* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَحْياكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَكَفُورٌ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to forbid the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from paying attention to their talk and from letting them dispute with him, in order to make him firm and spur his resolve to carry on with the matter Allah had entrusted to him. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) the khabar (predicate); the clause (أحياكم) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (يميتكم) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. when the appointed terms end; (ثم) is a conjunction, also of delay; (يحييكم) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the kāf is its object, i.e. at the resurrection. The clause (إن الإنسان لكفور) is resumptive, giving the reason for the failure to take heed and see after these lessons and proofs; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (كفور) is its khabar. (لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنا مَنْسَكاً هُمْ ناسِكُوهُ فَلا يُنازِعُنَّكَ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَادْعُ إِلى رَبِّكَ إِنَّكَ لَعَلى هُدىً مُسْتَقِيمٍ) (لكل أمة) is the fronted second object of (جعلنا) and (منسكا) is the first object. The clause is resumptive, with no connection to what precedes it, which is why the resumptive wāw was not brought; it is brought to rebuke those of the people of the heavenly religions who disputed with him. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (ناسكوه) the khabar, and the nominal clause is a naʿt (adjective) of (منسكا). The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa); (لا) is prohibitive; (ينازعنك) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because of the succession of like letters; the wāw dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents is the wāw of the plural, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it has not affected the inflection of the imperfect [making it indeclinable], because it is not directly attached to it — parallels of this have passed. The kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; (في الأمر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينازعنك). (ادع) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil being "you"; (إلى ربك) is attached to (ادع), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. to His religion and His path. The clause (إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم) is causal, with no grammatical position; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; (على هدى) is its khabar and (مستقيم) a naʿt of (هدى). (وَإِنْ جادَلُوكَ فَقُلِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (جادلوك) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi. (فقل): the fāʾ is linking and (قل) is an imperative verb; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعلم) the khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause (فقل) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (بما) is attached to (أعلم) and (تعملون) is the ṣila. (اللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فِيما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ) A resumptive clause brought to console the Prophet for what he used to meet. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحكم) its khabar; (بينكم) is an adverb attached to (يحكم), and (يوم القيامة) is also attached to (يحكم); (فيما) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila; (كان) and its noun; (فيه) is attached to (تختلفون), and the clause (تختلفون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); (لم) is a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; (تعلم) is an imperfect verb, jussive, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (أن) and what falls in its domain stand in place of the two objects of (يعلم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb meant is (تعلم)]; (أن) and its noun, and the clause (يعلم) is its khabar; (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi; (في السماء) is the ṣila of (ما) and (الأرض) is conjoined to (السماء). (إِنَّ ذلِكَ فِي كِتابٍ إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ) Two clauses giving the reason for what preceded: (إن) and its noun, with (في كتاب) its khabar; and (إن) and its noun, with (يسير) its khabar; (على الله) is attached to (يسير).

dervis-irab:30-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حُرُماتِ اللَّهِ): الحرمات, with two ḍammas; in the plural one also says حرمات, with ḍamma then fatḥa, and حرم, with ḍamma then fatḥa; the plural of حرمة, with ḍamma then sukūn, حرمة with two ḍammas, and حرمة with ḍamma then fatḥa. It is the covenant of protection, reverence, the rights of Allah that must be upheld and whose neglect is forbidden, and what may not be violated. The details of the حرمات are taken from the books of jurisprudence.
(الرِّجْسَ): with doubled, kasra-vowelled rāʾ and sukūn on the jīm; and الرَّجَس, with doubled, fatḥa-vowelled rāʾ and fatḥa on the jīm; and الرَّجِس, with doubled, fatḥa-vowelled rāʾ and kasra on the jīm: filth and dirt. He called the idols رجس by way of simile, because they are a moral filth.
(الزُّورِ): associating partners with Allah, falsehood and lying. Among its meanings also are intellect and strength — one says ما له زور ولا صيّور, that is, he has no strength and no recourse; and opinion; the chief and leader; the pleasure and good taste of food; the softness and cleanness of a garment; and a gathering for singing. It is from الزور or it is الازورار, which is deviation. In al-Asās: "A زوراء word: base and crooked; a زوراء minaret: leaning from the vertical; he shot with the زوراء: with the bow; a زوراء desert; he is أزور (turning away) from the station of abasement. You say: a people turned away (زور) from the stands of truth: their action is showing-off and their speech is falsehood (زور). Why do you worship the زور? — which is everything worshipped besides Allah. And I make my praise visit you (أزيركم), and I made my odes visit you (أزرتكم)." Someone has versified the meanings of this root in the following lines:
الصّدر والزائر فهو زور ... وكلّ زوار النساء زير
في جمع أزور يقال زور ... أعني به ذا ميل في الصدر
زيارة أي مرة فزوره ... وهيئة الزيارة ادع زيره
وقطعة الكتان أما الزّوره ... فموضع ذو شجر وطين
(The chest and the visitor: that is زور; and every frequent visitor of women is a زير; for the plural of أزور one says زور — I mean by it one with a slant in the chest; one visit is a زورة, and the manner of visiting call زيرة; and a piece of linen…; as for الزّورة, it is a place with trees and mud.)
Baghdad was called al-Zawrāʾ because of the deviation of its qibla. Al-Ṭughrāʾī said:
فيم الإقامة بالزوراء لا سكني ... بها ولا ناقتي فيها ولا جملي
(Why stay on in al-Zawrāʾ, where there is neither my abode, nor my she-camel, nor my camel?)
(فَتَخْطَفُهُ): in al-Qāmūs: خطف يخطف, of the pattern تعب, خطفا الشيء: he snatched the thing quickly; خطف البرق البصر: the lightning took away the sight quickly.
(سَحِيقٍ): far, that is, so his rescue is not hoped for.
(شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ): the plural of شعيرة or شعارة with kasra. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "And the شعائر are the landmarks of the pilgrimage and its acts; the singular is شعيرة or شعارة with kasra; and the مشاعر are the places of the rites."

* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ حُرُماتِ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ): ذلك: al-Zamakhsharī said: "The khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, the matter and the affair is that — just as the writer sets out a portion of his book on some topic, then when he wants to plunge into another topic he says: 'This (هذا); and it was such-and-such.'" The meaning of this is that it is mentioned to separate between two discourses or between two aspects of one discourse. It is also said: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, that is the matter which I mentioned; and it is said: in the position of accusative, its implied form being "comply with that". The like of this eloquent demonstrative is the saying of Zuhayr describing Harim ibn Sinān:
هذا وليس كمن يعيا بخطبته ... وسط النديّ إذا ما ناطق نطقا
(This (is he); and he is not like one who is tongue-tied in his oration in the midst of the assembly when a speaker speaks.)
He had described him before this with generosity and courage, then described him in this verse with eloquence, so it is as though he said: this is his character, and he is not like one who is tongue-tied in his oration.
The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussivising conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يعظم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its agent is latent, referring to من; حرمات الله is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fāʾ links; هو is a mubtadaʾ and خير a khabar; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. عند ربه: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ الْأَنْعامُ إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; أحلت is a passive past verb; لكم is attached to أحلت; الأنعام is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). إلا is a particle of exception; and ما is the excepted, in which both the connected and the disconnected (exception) are possible. The i'rab of this verse has preceded, together with what Allah excepted in His Book. The disconnected (exception) is on the basis that the verse of al-Māʾida mentions what is not of the genus of livestock, such as blood and the flesh of swine; and the connected is on the basis of referring it to what is forbidden of livestock because of an accidental cause, such as dying (unslaughtered) and the like. The clause يتلى is the ṣila (relative clause), and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun; عليكم is attached to يتلى.
(فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثانِ وَاجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ): the fāʾ is of derivation (tafrīʿ) from His saying ومن يعظم حرمات الله. اجتنبوا الرجس is an imperative verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi; من الأوثان is an explication of الرجس, so it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that it be a tamyīz (specification), and he illustrated that with your saying "I have twenty of the dirhams", because the الرجس among them covers more than one thing, as though it were said: so avoid the filth which is the idols. His view is not far-fetched. واجتنبوا قول الزور is conjoined to what precedes.
(حُنَفاءَ لِلَّهِ غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِ): حنفاء لله is a foundational ḥāl (ḥāl muʾassisa) from the pronoun of اجتنبوا, and غير مشركين is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), also from it; به is attached to مشركين. Their discussion will come in the Benefits section.
(وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّما خَرَّ مِنَ السَّماءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ الطَّيْرُ أَوْ تَهْوِي بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي مَكانٍ سَحِيقٍ): this sentence is resumptive, set out to strike a likeness for whoever associates partners with Allah. من is a jussivising conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ, and يشرك بالله is the protasis. فكأنما: the fāʾ links, and كأنما is a restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) (particle); خر is a past verb with a latent agent; من السماء is attached to خرّ. فتخطفه is conjoined to خرّ; it turned to the imperfect only for a secret that will come in the Rhetoric section. الطير is the agent; أو تهوي به الريح is also conjoined; في مكان is also attached to تهوي, and سحيق is a naʿt (adjective) of مكان.
(ذلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّها مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ): ذلك is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as preceded; the i'rab of ومن يعظم شعائر الله has preceded. The fāʾ links; إنّ with its noun, and من تقوى القلوب is its khabar.
(لَكُمْ فِيها مَنافِعُ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ مَحِلُّها إِلَى الْبَيْتِ الْعَتِيقِ): لكم is a fronted khabar; فيها is a ḥāl; منافع is a postponed mubtadaʾ; إلى أجل is a naʿt of منافع, and مسمى a naʿt of أجل. ثم is a conjunction; محلها is a mubtadaʾ, and it is a noun of place from حلّ يحلّ, that is, it became lawful; إلى البيت is the khabar, and العتيق a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
1- The composite and allegorical simile (al-tashbīh al-murakkab wa-l-tamthīlī). It has preceded that it is that in which the point of resemblance is an image drawn from multiple things. The explanation of that is that since the state of the unbeliever is divided into two kinds, beyond which there is no more: the first of them is the wavering doubter who persists in doubt and has not resolved on a single error. This kind of polytheist is likened to one whom the birds have snatched and divided among themselves, so that no bird takes possession of a shred of him without another plundering it from him; and that is the state of the waverer: no phantom appears to him without his following it and abandoning what he was on. The second is a polytheist resolved on a false belief, who, were he sawn with saws, would not retreat from his resolve; there is no way to make him doubt, and no hope of moving him from what he is on, so he is glad and delighted with his error. This one, in his persistence in his disbelief, is likened to the settledness of one whom the wind has flung down into a far, low valley, and he has settled in it; and the counterpart is likening him to settling in the far valley, which is the farthest possible from the sky [Translator's note: this last clause is as written and appears incomplete].
Al-Zamakhsharī permitted this simile to be of the composite and of the separate (mufarraq) kind. He said: "If it is a composite simile, it is as though He said: whoever associates partners with Allah has destroyed himself with a destruction beyond which there is no end, by depicting his state in the image of the state of one who fell from the sky, and the birds snatched him and he was scattered in shreds in their crops, or the wind blew him violently until it flung him down into some distant place of casting. And if it is separate, He has likened faith, in its loftiness, to the sky; the one who left faith and associated partners with Allah to the one falling from the sky; the whims that divide his thoughts to the snatching birds; and the devil who flings him into the valley of error to the wind that flings what it blows into some ruinous abyss."
Al-Zamakhsharī's statement is open to question, because it is an allegorical simile, there is no doubt in that, and there is no room for making it separate.
2- Turning to the imperfect form:
The context of the speech requires that فتخطفه be conjoined to an imperfect, although in the verse it is conjoined to خر, which is past. It turned away from that only to depict the reality, the implied form being "so it snatches him", so that it would be a conjunction of clause to clause. But He preferred the divergence to bring to mind the strange image that depicts him in shreds in the crops of the birds.

* Benefits:
1- The ḥāl is either foundational (muʾassisa) or emphatic (muʾakkida). The foundational is that whose meaning is not obtained without it, as in جاء خالد راكبا (Khālid came riding); most ḥāls come of this kind. The emphatic is that whose meaning is obtained without it, and it is brought only for emphasis. These are of three kinds:
a- That which is brought to emphasise its governor, namely that which agrees with it in meaning only, or in meaning and wording. The first is as in "تبسم ضاحكا" (he smiled, laughing); and of it is the saying of the Exalted «وَلا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ». The second is as in the saying of the Exalted «وَأَرْسَلْناكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولًا», and the saying of the poet:
أصخ مصيخا لمن أبدى نصيحته ... والزم توقي خلط الجد باللعب
(Listen attentively to whoever offers his counsel, and hold fast to guarding against mixing earnest with jest.)
b- That which is brought to emphasise its owner (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), as in the saying of the Exalted «وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً».
c- That which is brought to emphasise the content of a clause composed of two definite, inflexible (jāmid) nouns, as in هو الحق بيّنا or صريحا (it is the truth, evident / plain), and the saying of the poet:
أنا ابن دارة معروفا بها نسبي ... وهل بدارة يا للناس من عار
(I am the son of Dāra, my lineage known by her — and is there, O people, any shame in Dāra?)
2- Why the pronoun in فإنها is feminine:
In the saying of the Exalted «وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّها مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ» there is an important question: why was the pronoun made feminine, and to what does it refer? The answer is not sound except by supposing omitted muḍāfs, and the meaning is not sound except by supposing them, because the pronoun refers to the شعائر, that is: for venerating them is among the acts of the piety of hearts; and the resumptive pronoun referring to من is omitted, that is, "from him". It is also possible that the pronoun is the pronoun of a feminine maṣdar, its implied form being: for the veneration, or the sanctity, or the trait (is…).

dervis-irab:34-38.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَنْسَكاً): with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn. The fatḥa is on the basis that it is a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun), and the kasra on the basis that it is a noun of place. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "نسك لله ينسك, of the pattern قتل: he performed a voluntary act of devotion; and النسك, with two ḍammas, is the noun from it; in the Revelation: «إِنَّ صَلاتِي وَنُسُكِي». المنسك, with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn, may be a time and a maṣdar, and may be the noun of the place in which the نسيكة is slaughtered, which is the ذبيحة (sacrificial animal) in measure and meaning. The مناسك of the pilgrimage are its acts of worship; it is also said: the places of the acts of worship. Whoever does such-and-such owes a نسك, that is, blood that he sheds. نسك: he lived ascetically and devoted himself to worship, so he is ناسك, and the plural is نساك, like عابد and عباد." In al-Qāmūs: "المنسك, with fatḥa on the sīn, is the familiar place; المنسك, also with fatḥa, is the maṣdar of نسك; and المنسك, with kasra, is the law of the rite and a place in which the نسيكة is slaughtered."
(الْمُخْبِتِينَ): the obedient, the humble. الإخبات is descending into the خبت, which is low-lying ground. A valuable discussion of this description will come in the Rhetoric section [Translator's note: no Rhetoric section follows in this entry of the source].
(الْبُدْنَ): with ḍamma on the bāʾ, the plural of بدنة; they were so called because of the bulk of their bodies (بدن). It is specific to camels, as al-Azharī said, or it includes camels and cattle, as the author of al-Ṣiḥāḥ said. Al-Qasṭallānī said: "البدن, according to al-Shāfiʿī, is specific to camels, and according to Abū Ḥanīfa it is of camels and cattle; so the statement of the Shāfiʿīs agrees with the statement of al-Azharī, and the statement of the Ḥanafīs agrees with the statement of al-Ṣiḥāḥ."
(صَوافَّ): standing, having lined up their forelegs and hind legs. It was also read صوافن, from صفون الفرس, which is that the horse stands on three legs and sets the fourth upright on the tip of its hoof; because the sacrificial camel has one of its forelegs hobbled.
(وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُها): the وجوب of the sides is their falling to the ground, from وجب الحائط وجبة when the wall fell, and وجبت الشمس وجبة: the sun set. Abū Tammām said:
فالشمس طالعة من ذا وقد غربت ... والشمس واجبة من ذا ولم تجب
(So the sun is rising from this one though it has set, and the sun is setting from this one though it has not set.)
(الْقانِعَ): the beggar who abases himself; one who goes from place to place; the servant of the people and their hireling; the plural is قانعون and قنّع. Or it has the sense of القنع, that is, the one content with what is allotted to him. One says قنع يقنع, of the pattern تعب تعبا, قنعا, قناعة and قنعانا: he was content with what was allotted to him. One says قنع يقنع, of the pattern تعب تعبا: قنعا, قناعة and قنعانا: he was content with what was allotted to him [Translator's note: this sentence is repeated thus in the source]. And قنع يقنع, of the pattern فتح, قنوعا: he begged and abased himself. In al-Asās and al-Lisān: "Honour lies in contentment (القناعة) and abasement in begging (القنوع), which is asking. So-and-so is قنع with (his) livelihood, and قنيع, قنوع and قانع. Al-Kisāʾī recited:
فإن ملكت كفاك قوطا فكن به ... قنيعا فإن المتقي الله قانع
(If your two palms possess a little flock, be content with it, for the one who fears Allah is content.)
And قنع بالشيء, اقتنع and تقنّع (he was content with the thing); and may Allah make you content (أقنعك) with what He has given you; and so-and-so is greedy, nothing contents him." And Shawqī's famous verse:
شباب قنع لا خير فيهم ... وبورك بالشباب الطامحينا
(Youths who are content (with little) — there is no good in them; and blessed be the aspiring youths!)
indicates his mastery of the language and his command of it.
(الْمُعْتَرَّ): the one who presents himself by asking; عرّه and عراه have one meaning. It is said that القانع is the one who asks and المعتر the one who presents himself without asking; and some said the reverse. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "المعتر is the visiting guest; and المعتر is the one who presents himself for asking without requesting. One says عرّه, اعترّه, عراه and اعتراه when he presented himself for a favour without asking." In al-Qāmūs: "And المعتر is the poor man, and the one who presents himself for a favour without asking; عرّه عرّا, and اعترّه, and (اعترّ) به." In al-Asās and al-Lisān: "And from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: the orphan's property is a عرّة (a blight); I do not bring it into my property nor mix it with it. Do not do this, lest a disgrace (معرّة) befall you from it. In the hadith: 'Whenever I woke at night (تعاررت), I remembered Allah.' And Salmān, may Allah be pleased with him, when he woke in the night (تعارّ) would say: 'Glory be to the Lord of the prophets and the God of the messengers'; and it is that one starts up from sleep with speech — from عرار الظليم, which is the cry of the male ostrich. And «أطعموا القانع والمعتر», that is, the one who presents himself with his asking."

* I'rab:
(وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنا مَنْسَكاً لِيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلى ما رَزَقَهُمْ مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعامِ): the wāw is resumptive; the sentence is resumptive, set out to establish the law specific to each nation and the kind of worship by which they draw near to Allah. لكل أمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element that is the fronted second object of جعلنا; جعلنا is a verb and agent; منسكا is the first object of جعلنا. ليذكروا: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and يذكروا is an imperfect made accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation; the preposition and its genitive (clause) are attached to جعلنا. اسم الله is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); على ما رزقهم is attached to يذكروا; the clause رزقهم is the ṣila (relative clause); من بهيمة الأنعام is attached to رزقهم.
(فَإِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ فَلَهُ أَسْلِمُوا وَبَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied clause); إلهكم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and إله its khabar (predicate); واحد is a naʿt (adjective). فله: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and له is attached to أسلموا; أسلموا is an imperative verb and agent. وبشر: the wāw is a conjunction; بشر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; المخبتين is a mafʿūl bihi.
(الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَالصَّابِرِينَ عَلى ما أَصابَهُمْ وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ): الذين is a naʿt of المخبتين or a badal (substitute) of it. إذا is an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the clause ذكر الله is in a genitive construct with it; the clause وجلت قلوبهم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; إذا with its verb and apodosis has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. الصابرين is conjoined to الذين; على ما is attached to الصابرين; the clause أصابهم is the ṣila of the relative noun. المقيمي الصلاة is also conjoined, the nūn having been dropped because of the annexation. مما is attached to ينفقون; the clause رزقناهم is a ṣila, and the clause ينفقون is also a ṣila.
(وَالْبُدْنَ جَعَلْناها لَكُمْ مِنْ شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; البدن is the object of an omitted verb, so it is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), that is: and We made the sacrificial camels. جعلناها is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi; لكم is attached to جعلناها; من شعائر الله is the second mafʿūl bihi of جعلناها, which is in the sense of "making into".
(لَكُمْ فِيها خَيْرٌ فَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها صَوافَّ): لكم is a fronted khabar; فيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); خير is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The sentence is resumptive, set out to establish what precedes it; it may be made a ḥāl from the hāʾ in جعلناها. فاذكروا: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; اذكروا is an imperative verb and agent; اسم الله is a mafʿūl bihi; عليها is attached to اذكروا; صواف is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, that is, side by side.
(فَإِذا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُها فَكُلُوا مِنْها وَأَطْعِمُوا الْقانِعَ وَالْمُعْتَرَّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb of time; the clause وجبت جنوبها is in a genitive construct with the adverb; the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; the clause كلوا منها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; وأطعموا القانع والمعتر is conjoined to the clause كلوا منها.
(كَذلِكَ سَخَّرْناها لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): كذلك: the kāf is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, that is, He subjected them with a subjection like that subjection. سخرناها is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl; لكم is attached to سخرناها. لعلّ with its noun, and the clause تشكرون is its khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf in لكم.
(لَنْ يَنالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُها وَلا دِماؤُها وَلكِنْ يَنالُهُ التَّقْوى مِنْكُمْ): لن is a particle of negation, accusative and future; ينال is an imperfect verb made accusative by لن; the Majestic Name is a fronted mafʿūl bihi; لحومها is the agent of ينال; ولا دماؤها is conjoined to لحومها. The meaning is: they will not attain His good pleasure and will not find acceptance with Him; and what is meant is the owners of the flesh and blood. Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: "The Muslims wanted to do as the polytheists did, slaughtering and setting up strips of meat around the Kaʿba and smearing the Kaʿba with blood, seeking nearness to Allah the Exalted; so this verse was revealed." ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened; يناله is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi; التقوى is the agent; منكم is a ḥāl from التقوى, that is: there is raised to Him from you the righteous deed done purely for Him, with faith.
(كَذلِكَ سَخَّرَها لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلى ما هَداكُمْ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the kāf is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, and its likes have preceded. سخرها is a past verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi; لكم is attached to سخرها. لتكبروا: the lām is for causation, and تكبروا is accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation; the lām and what is in its scope are attached to سخرها; تكبروا is an imperfect verb and agent, and the Majestic Name is a mafʿūl bihi. على ما هداكم: ما is maṣdar-forming or relative, that is, for His guiding you, or for what He has guided you to; على is attached to تكبروا because it is made to contain the sense of thanking. وبشر: the wāw is resumptive; بشر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, and المؤمنين [Translator's note: as written; the verse has المحسنين] is a mafʿūl bihi.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدافِعُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ كَفُورٍ): a resumptive sentence set out to confirm the glad tidings to the believers of certain victory. إن الله: إنّ with its noun, and the clause يدافع is the khabar; عن الذين is attached to يدافع; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. The object of يدافع is omitted, its implied form being: the aggressions of the polytheists and their evil plots. The clause إن الذين [Translator's note: as written; the clause is إن الله لا يحب] gives the reason for the preceding clause: إنّ with its noun, and the clause لا يحب is its khabar; كل خوان is a mafʿūl bihi, and كفور is a naʿt of خوان.

dervis-irab:71-74.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَسْطُونَ): they assault. Al-saṭw is leaping and assaulting, which is why it is made transitive with the bāʾ; otherwise it is made transitive with (على): one says "saṭā ʿalayhi". Its root meaning is overpowering and prevailing. In al-Asās: «Saṭā bi-qirnihi and ʿalā qirnihi: he leapt upon his rival and assaulted him; the stallion saṭā upon his mate.
