Among the figurative uses: the water saṭā, it increased and swelled; "I did not saṭawtu in anyone's food": I did not partake of it; and "they have hands sawāṭ ʿawāṭ" [i.e. hands that reach out and take]. Al-Mutanakhkhil said describing wine:
ركود في الإناء لها حميّا ... تلذّ بأخذها الأيدي السواطي
(Still in the vessel, it has a fiery strength; the reaching hands delight in taking it.)
The sīn with the ṭāʾ, as the first and second radicals of a word, carries the property of extension. You say: "I saw them sitting on the masāṭib", which are the benches extending around the courtyard of the mosque; "so-and-so spent the night on the misṭaba"; and you say: "How many men has this house made to spend the night on the benches, and cast into perils and ruin!", meaning "so travel through Allah's lands". And you say: "Either he makes you spend the night on the misṭaba, or he raises you to the misṭaba", which is the Milky Way. Saṭaḥa the thing:
he spread it out and levelled it; from it "he spread the bread with the misṭaḥ", which is the rolling pin, and "he spread the tharīd in the bowl"; from it is the saṭḥ (roof) of the house; "a musaṭṭaḥ surface": level; "a musaṭṭaḥ nose": very flat; "he spread out for us the misṭaḥ and the masāṭiḥ", which is a mat of palm leaves; "he struck him and saṭaḥahu" when he threw him flat on his back stretched out, so he became flattened (insaṭaḥa), and he is saṭīḥ and munsaṭiḥ — after this Saṭīḥ was named; "he struck him with the misṭaḥ", which is the tent pole; "he drank from the saṭīḥa", which is the water-skin. Saṭara and istaṭara: he wrote; "he wrote a saṭr of his book", and saṭr, asṭur, suṭūr and asṭār; "he is musayṭir over us" and mutasayṭir. "An extended, rising (sāṭiʿa) fire", "a shining (sāṭiʿ) light"; the dawn saṭaʿa, the dust saṭaʿa, suṭūʿan; the camel and the male ostrich saṭaʿa: stretched its neck towards the sky. Dhū al-Rumma said describing a male ostrich:
يظلّ مختضعا طورا فتنكره ... حينا ويسطع أحيانا فينتسب
(He keeps lowering his head at one time, so that you fail to recognise him for a while, and at times he stretches his neck up, and so declares his lineage.)
Saṭaʿa with his hands: he raised them, clapping with them. Among the figurative uses: the scent of musk saṭaʿat (spread), and "the diffusion of its scent pleased me". "I washed with the saṭl and the sayṭal", which are the vessel [Translator's note: the text has «القدس»] with which one purifies oneself in the bath. "He stirred the fire with the isṭām", and "a sword with a polished siṭām", which is the edge. Sībawayh cited, by Kaʿb ibn Juʿayl:
وأبيض مصقول السطام مهنّدا ... وذا حلق من نسج داود مسردا
(And a white Indian blade with polished edge, and a ringed coat of mail of David's weaving, closely riveted.)
Among the figurative uses: "a night whose usṭumma (thick middle) swelled", "he is in the usṭumma of Quraysh": in their midst; "the kingship returned to its usṭumma": to its root. He said:
يا ليتها قد خرجت من فمّه ... حتى يعود الملك في اسطمّه
(Would that it had come out of his mouth, so that the kingship might return to its root.)
And the Arabs are the siṭām (edge, i.e. the best) of people.»
(الذُّبابُ): a generic noun whose singular is dhubāba; it applies to male and female; it is pluralised as dhibbān with kasra, like ghirbān, as dhubbān with ḍamma, like quḍbān, and as adhibba, like aghriba. It is the most ignorant of animals, because it throws itself into fatal places. Its lifespan is forty days; its creation originates from putrefactions, then it reproduces one from another. Its droppings fall on something white and appear black, and on something black and appear white. Dhubāb is taken from "dhabba" when one drives away and "āba" when one returns, because you drive it away and it comes back to you. Imruʾ al-Qays mentioned it in his poetry, saying:
أرانا موضعين لأمر غيب ... ونسحر بالطعام وبالشراب
(I see us hastening towards a hidden matter, and we are beguiled by food and drink —)
عصافير وذبّان ودود ... وأجرأ من مجلّحة الذئاب
(sparrows, flies and worms, yet bolder than the most daring of wolves.)
An extensive discussion of it will come in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطاناً) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive. (يعبدون) is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (لم ينزل) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); (به) is a ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of (سلطانا); and (سلطانا) is the mafʿūl bihi. (وَما لَيْسَ لَهُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ نَصِيرٍ) (وما) is conjoined to the first (ما); the clause (ليس) is the ṣila; (لهم) is the fronted khabar (predicate) of (ليس); (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (علم); (علم) is the delayed noun of (ليس). (وما): the wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative; (للظالمين) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (نصير) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْمُنْكَرَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause (تتلى) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذا) to it; (تتلى) is an imperfect passive verb; (عليهم) is attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and (بينات) a ḥāl. The clause (تعرف) has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of (إذا); (في وجوه) is attached to (تعرف); (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (المنكر) is the mafʿūl bihi. In it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, namely (الذين كفروا), to denounce them and to record the testimony against them of disbelief. (يَكادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِالَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِنا) The clause (يكادون) is a ḥāl of the relative noun, even though it is in the genitive by annexation, because the muḍāf is a part of it; it may be a ḥāl of (وجوه), because what is meant by it is their owners. (يكادون) is one of the verbs of approximation; the wāw is its noun and the clause (يسطون) its khabar; (بالذين) is attached to (يسطون); the clause (يتلون) is the ṣila; (عليهم) is attached to (يتلون) and (آياتنا) is the mafʿūl bihi.
(قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذلِكُمُ النَّارُ) (قل) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive. (أفأنبئكم): the hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "Shall I address you and inform you?"; (أنبئكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (بشر) is attached to (أنبئكم) and (من ذلكم) is attached to (شر). (النار) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; or (النار) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (وعدها), and the clause has no grammatical position because it explains (شر). (وَعَدَهَا اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) The clause (وعدها الله) is either a second khabar or the khabar of (النار). (وعدها الله) is a verb, its first object and its fāʿil, and (الذين كفروا) is the second object of (وعدها); it may be that the pronoun is the second object and (الذين كفروا) the first object, and perhaps this is preferable, for a reason that will come in the Benefits section. (وبئس المصير) is a verb and its fāʿil, and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "it". (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ) Resumptive speech brought to strike the parable; although it is more like a story, it is called a mathal because of its currency and its strangeness. The iʿrāb of (يا أيها الناس) has been given many times. (ضرب مثل) is a past passive verb and its nāʾib fāʿil. (فاستمعوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa); (استمعوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (له) is attached to (استمعوا). (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُباباً وَلَوِ اجْتَمَعُوا لَهُ) The clause explains the parable. (إن) and its noun; the clause (تدعون) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; the clause (لن يخلقوا ذبابا) is the khabar of (إن) and (ذبابا) is the mafʿūl bihi. (ولو): the wāw conjoins to something omitted that is a ḥāl, i.e. their creating a fly is negated in every state, even in this state in which they have gathered for it; (لو) is conditional; (اجتمعوا) is a verb and its fāʿil, and (له) is attached to (اجتمعوا). (وَإِنْ يَسْلُبْهُمُ الذُّبابُ شَيْئاً لا يَسْتَنْقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ضَعُفَ الطَّالِبُ وَالْمَطْلُوبُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (يسلبهم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi and (الذباب) the fāʿil; (شيئا) is the second object. (لا) is negative and (يستنقذوه) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi; (منه) is attached to (يستنقذوه). The clause (ضعف الطالب والمطلوب) is a ḥāl. And (ما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): the wāw is resumptive, brought to reply to the rabbis of the Jews and their leaders who said: Allah is poor and we are rich. (ما) is negative; (قدروا) is a verb and its fāʿil; the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi; (حق قدره) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause (إن الله …) gives the reason for what preceded; (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (قوي) is the first khabar of (إن) and (عزيز) the second khabar of (إن).

* Rhetoric:
Sound invention (salāmat al-ikhtirāʿ):
This is that the poet or writer invents a meaning to which he was not preceded and in which he did not follow anyone. His saying, Exalted is He, «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُباباً», the verse, is among the most eloquent things Allah revealed in exposing the ignorance of the disbelievers and the feebleness of their minds, because of the strangeness of the comparison, which contains extreme hyperbole while running according to the truth and issuing forth as truthfulness. That is when He, Glorified is He, confined Himself to mentioning the weakest of creatures and the least in what it takes away, and declared everyone apart from Him, Glorified is He, whoever he may be, incapable of creating its like even with mutual support and gathering together. Then in the comparison He descended from the rank of creating — since these two are things whose like every powerful one other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is incapable of — to recovering the trifling, worthless thing which this weak creature, for all its weakness, takes away, and which every powerful one among the creatures is incapable of recovering from it. So He moved down step by step in the comparison as eloquence requires in this place, in order. Since He, Glorified is He, knew that there was no hyperbole in declaring them incapable of creating and inventing — which no tyrant claims and none of the creatures undertakes, even if he has been given power and granted strength and has in him such excess of disbelief and ignorance that he claims divinity and arrogates lordship — He brought them down to recovering what this weak creature takes away, for all its weakness and their strength, to show them their incapacity, so that their souls would be certain of it even if their tongues did not admit it. So He brought what outward appearance judges to be easier than creating, whereas in reality it is like it in [difficulty] [Translator's note: the text has «في العمر», apparently a misprint, perhaps for «في الأمر»]; for getting hold of this creature itself is easier than getting hold of what it takes away, so the incapacity to recover what it takes away is like [the incapacity to] create it. No such comparison of its kind was heard from anyone before the revelation of the Mighty Book.
The scholars of bayān have divided sound invention into two kinds:
The first: that which its author originates without following anyone who preceded him in it. This kind is hit upon at new events and noticed at sudden occurrences. Of this is what came in the poetry of Abū Tammām, in an ode in which he praises al-Muʿtaṣim bi-llāh and mentions the burning of al-Afshīn, whose opening is:
الحق أبلج والسيوف عوار ... فحذار من أسد العرين حذار
(Truth is radiant and swords are bare; so beware, beware the lion of the thicket!)
In it he invents a description of the crucified, saying:
بكروا وأسروا في متون ضوامر ... قيدت لهم من مربط النّجّار
(They set out at dawn and travelled by night on lean backs, led to them from the carpenter's stable.)
لا يبرحون ومن رآهم خالهم ... أبدا على سفر من الأسفار
(They do not move, yet whoever sees them imagines them forever on one of their journeys.)
This meaning is of the kind hit upon at new events; in such a situation the mind is led to the invented meaning without great effort, because of the evidence of the present state. And among what he said in it describing the one burnt with fire:
ما زال سر الكفر بين ضلوعه ... حتى اصطلى سرّ الزناد الواري
(The secret of disbelief remained between his ribs until he was roasted by the secret of the kindling fire-stick —)
نارا يساور جسمه من حرها ... لهب كما عصفرت شقّ إزار
(a fire from whose heat a flame leapt at his body, like a strip of wrap you have dyed with safflower.)
طارت لها شعل يهدّم لفحها ... أركانه هدما بغير غبار
(Its flames flew up, their blast demolishing his pillars, a demolition without dust.)
فصّلن منه كلّ مجمع مفصل ... وفعلن فاقرة بكل فقار
(They separated every joint of his, and wrought a backbreaking calamity on every vertebra.)
مشبوبة رفعت لأعظم مشرك ... ما كان يرفع ضوءها للساري
(A blazing fire raised for the greatest polytheist, whose light was not raised for the night traveller [i.e. not a fire of hospitality].)
صلى لها حيا وكان وقودها ... ميتا ويدخلها مع الفجار
(He was roasted by it alive and was its fuel dead, and he enters it [i.e. Hell] with the wicked.)
Al-Buḥturī appended to what Abū Tammām mentioned in describing the crucified, saying:
كم عزيز أباده فغدا ير ... كب عودا مركّبا في عود
(How many a mighty one he destroyed, who came to ride a wooden beam fixed upon a beam!)
أسلمته إلى الرقاد رجال ... لم يكونوا عن وترهم برقود
(Men delivered him over to sleep who did not sleep over their vengeance.)
تحسد الطير فيه ضبع البوادي ... وهو في غير حالة المحسود
(The hyenas of the desert envy the birds for him, though he is in no enviable state.)
غاب عن صحبه فلا هو موجو ... د لديهم وليس بالمفقود
(He is absent from his companions: neither present with them nor lost.)
وكأن امتداد كفيه فوق الجذع في محفل الردى المشهود طائر مدّ مستريحا جناحيه استراحات متعب مكدود
(It is as if the stretching of his hands over the trunk, in the attended assembly of death, were a bird spreading its wings at rest, the rest of one wearied and exhausted.)
أخطب الناس راكبا فإذا أر ... جل خاطبت منه عين البليد
(The most eloquent of people as a rider; but when he dismounted, you addressed in him the eye of a dullard.)
Of this kind is what came in the poetry of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī in his description of fever:
وزائرتي كأن بها حياء ... فليس تزور إلا في الظلام
(My visitor seems to be bashful, for she visits only in the dark.)
بذلت لها المطارف والحشايا ... فعافتها وباتت في عظامي
(I offered her silk wraps and cushions, but she spurned them and spent the night in my bones.)
كأن الصبح يطردها فتجري ... مدامعها بأربعة سجام
(As if the morning drives her away, and her tears flow from four pouring ducts.)
أراقب وقتها من غير شوق ... مراقبة المشوق المستهام
(I watch for her time without longing, with the watchfulness of the longing, love-crazed lover.)
Among the marvels he produced in this field: Sayf Allāh [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. Sayf al-Dawla] ibn Ḥamdān was encamped in the land of Diyār Bakr at the city of Mayyāfāriqīn, and the wind struck his tent; people took it as an evil omen and said various things about it. So Abū al-Ṭayyib praised him in an ode excusing the fall of the tent, the first of which is:
أينفع في الخيمة العذّل ... وتشمل من دهرها يشمل
(Are reproaches of any use with the tent, and does she enclose the one who encloses her whole age?)
And among that in which he excelled to the utmost, and which was counted among his imperishable rare pieces, is his saying:
تضيق بشخصك أرجاؤها ... ويركض في الواحد الجحفل
(Its sides are too narrow for your person, though a whole army could gallop in one of them.)
وتقصر ما كنت في جوفها ... وتركز فيها القنا الذّبّل
(And it falls short so long as you are inside it, though the slender lances are planted in it.)
وكيف تقوم على راحة ... كأن البحار لها أنمل
(And how can it stand over a palm whose fingertips are like the seas?)
فليت وقارك فرّقته ... وحملت أرضك ما تحمل
(Would that you had distributed your gravity, and loaded your earth with what it can bear;)
فصار الأنام به سادة ... وسدتهم بالذي يفضل
(then mankind would become lords by it, and you would lord over them with what is left over.)
رأت لون نورك في لونها ... كلون الغزالة لا يغسل
(It saw the colour of your light in its own colour, like the colour of the sun, which cannot be washed off,)
وأنّ لها شرفا باذخا ... وأن الخيام بها تخجل
(and that it has lofty nobility and that the [other] tents are put to shame by it.)
فلا تنكرنّ لها صرعة ... فمن فرح النفس ما يقتل
(So do not reproach it for a fall, for there is joy of the soul that kills.)
ولو بلّغ الناس ما بلّغت ... لخانتهم حولك الأرجل
(Had people attained what it attained, their legs would have betrayed them around you.)
ولما أمرت بتطنيبها ... أشيع بأنك لا ترحل
(When you ordered it to be fastened with ropes, it was rumoured that you would not move on;)
فما اعتمد الله تقويضها ... ولكن أشار بما تفعل
(so Allah did not intend its collapse, but rather indicated what you should do,)
وعرّف انك من همه ... وأنك في نصره ترفل
(and made known that you are among His concerns and that you are clothed in His support.)
فما العاندون وما أمّلوا ... وما الحاسدون وما قوّلوا
(So what are the obstinate and what they hoped, and what are the envious and what they alleged?)
هم يطلبون فمن أدركوا؟ ... وهم يكذبون فمن يقبل؟
(They seek, but whom have they overtaken? They lie, but who accepts?)
وهم يتمنّون ما يشتهون ... ومن دونه جدّك المقبل
(They wish for what they desire, but before it stands your advancing fortune.)
The invented meanings in it are plain to see, and it is merit enough for al-Mutanabbī to produce their like.
In the book al-Rawḍa by Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad — a book in which he collected and selected the poems of poets, beginning with Abū Nuwās and then those of his time — he said among what he cited of his poetry: He has a meaning to which, by consensus, he was not preceded, namely his saying:
تدار علينا الراح في عسجدية ... حبتها بأنواع التصاوير فارس
(Wine is passed around us in a golden cup that Persia has endowed with all kinds of images:)
قرارتها كسرى وفي جنباتها ... مها تدّريها بالقسيّ الفوارس
(at its bottom is Chosroes, and on its sides oryxes that horsemen stalk with bows.)
فللراح ما زرت عليه جيوبها ... وللماء ما دارت عليه القلانس
(To the wine belongs what their collars are buttoned over, and to the water what the caps go round.)
The meaning is invented, but — as al-Jāḥiẓ says — it is among observed meanings: this wine bore only a little water, and it filled the figures of this cup up to the place of their collars, and the water in it was little, to the extent of the caps on their heads; this is the narration of a state observed by sight.
The second: meanings drawn out without an observed state to be pictured; these are harder to attain than what is drawn out with an observed state. It has been said that Abū Tammām is the most original of the later poets in meanings; his original meanings were counted and found to exceed twenty meanings:
Of these is his saying:
يا أيها الملك النائي برؤيته ... وجوده لمراعي جوده كثب
(O king, remote in being seen, while his bounty is near to those who graze on his bounty:)
ليس الحجاب بمقص عنك لي أملا ... إن السماء ترجّى حين تحتجب
(the veil does not put my hope in you at a distance; the sky is hoped for [rain] when it is veiled [by clouds].)
Likewise his saying in satire:
وأنت تدير قطب رحى عليا ... ولم نر للرحى العلياء قطبا
(You turn the pivot of an upper millstone, though we have never seen a pivot for the upper millstone.)
ترى ظفرا بكل صراع قرن ... إذا ما كنت أسفل منه جنبا
(You count it victory in every wrestling with a rival when you are lying beneath him.)
Likewise his saying:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
(When Allah wishes to spread a virtue that has been folded away, He provides for it the tongue of an envier;)
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(were it not for the fire's blazing in what it touches, the fragrance of aloeswood would not be known.)
Likewise he has, on grey hair:
شعلة في المفارق استودعتني ... في صميم الفؤاد ثكلا صميما
(A flame in the parting of the hair has deposited in the core of my heart a bereavement to the core.)
يستثير الهموم ما اكتنّ منها ... صعدا وهي تستثير الهموما
(Cares stir up what is hidden of it, rising, while it stirs up cares.)
However, Ibn al-Rūmī surpassed all the poets of Arabic in creating forms for abstract meanings, or creating symbols for some perceptible forms; indeed by it he surpassed all the poets of the world. Listen to his description of the motion of the thin bread in the baker's hand:
ما أنس لا أنس خبازا مررت به ... يدحو الرقاقة مثل اللمح بالبصر
(Whatever I forget, I shall not forget a baker I passed, spreading the thin loaf in the twinkling of an eye:)
ما بين رؤيتها في كفه كرة ... وبين رؤيتها قوراء كالقمر
(between seeing it in his palm as a ball and seeing it round and wide like the moon)
إلا بمقدار ما تنداح دائرة ... في صفحة الماء يرمى فيه بالحجر
(is only as long as it takes a circle to spread on the surface of water into which a stone is thrown.)
And his description of the slow motion in the progress of the clouds:
سحائب قيست في البلاد فألفيت ... غطاء على أغوارها ونجودها
(Clouds measured over the lands and found to be a covering over their lowlands and highlands;)
حدتها النّعامى مثقلات فأقبلت ... تهادى، رويدا، سيرها كركودها
(the south wind drove them, heavy-laden, and they came swaying gently, their moving like their standing still.)
And he has:
وإذا امرؤ مدح امرأ لنواله ... وأطال فيه فقد أراد هجاءه
(When a man praises a man for his gifts and is lengthy in it, he has meant to satirise him;)
لو لم يقدر فيه بعد المستقى ... عند الورود لما أطال رشاءه
(had he not reckoned the well deep to draw from when coming to water, he would not have lengthened his rope.)
And he has his delightful saying:
عدوك من صديقك مستفاد ... فلا تستكثرنّ من الصحاب
(Your enemy is acquired from your friend, so do not gather many companions;)
فإن الداء أكثر ما تراه ... يكون من الطعام والشراب
(for disease, mostly as you see it, comes from food and drink.)
Likewise his saying:
لما تؤذن الدنيا به من صروفها ... يكون بكاء الطفل ساعة يولد
(Because of the vicissitudes the world announces to him, the child cries the moment he is born;)
وإلا فما يبكيه منها وانها ... لأوسع مما كان فيه وأرغد
(otherwise, what makes him cry at it, when it is wider and more comfortable than where he was?)
إذا أبصر الدنيا استهل كأنه ... بما هو لاق من أذاها يهدد
(When he sees the world he cries out, as though he were being threatened with the harm of it he will meet.)
A comprehensive statement by al-Jāḥiẓ:
Al-Jāḥiẓ has a delightful section in which he ends up describing the fly, which we are speaking about. He said: «No poet on earth is known to have come first with an apt, complete simile, or a strange, wondrous meaning, or a noble, generous meaning, or an invented novelty, but that every poet who came after him or with him — if he could not manage its wording, he steals some of it or claims it entirely — does not fail to seek help from the meaning and make himself a partner in it, like the meaning the poets contend over, their wordings and the metres of their poems differing, and none of them being more entitled to that meaning than his fellow; or perhaps he denies that he ever heard of that meaning and says: it occurred to my mind without hearing, as it occurred to the mind of the first — that is if they confront him with it — except for what came from ʿAntara in describing the fly: he described it and described it excellently, so all the poets avoided his meaning and did not attempt it. ʿAntara said:
جادت عليها كلّ عين ثرّة ... فتركن كل حديقة كالدرهم
(Every abundant rain-cloud poured generously upon it, leaving every garden like a dirham;)
فترى الذباب بها يغني وحده ... هزجا كفعل الشارب المترنّم
(and you see the fly in it singing alone, humming like the act of a tipsy drinker crooning;)
غردا يحكّ ذراعه بذراعه ... فعل المكبّ على الزناد الأجذم
(warbling, rubbing its forearm against its forearm, like the act of the handless man bent over the fire-sticks.)
He means the act of the one with amputated hands bent over the fire-sticks; al-ajdham is the one with both hands cut off. So he described the fly when it has settled and then rubs one of its hands with the other, and likened it at that moment to a man with both hands cut off striking fire with two sticks; and whenever the fly alights, it does that.»
The story of the judge of Basra:
After al-Jāḥiẓ, as is his habit in digression, had spoken at length about the fly, he narrated the story of the judge of Basra, which is long and depicts the insistence of the fly and its ability to bite. It is recorded in al-Jāḥiẓ's Kitāb al-Ḥayawān, so whoever wishes may refer to it.

* Benefits:
Whenever, after a verb that is transitive to two objects, two things come together, the second of which is not an expression for the first, then the one that is the agent in meaning has the rank of being placed first, and it is the first object; by the first object is meant the one from whom an action can come. So if you say "I promised Zayd a dinar", the dinar is the second object, because no action can come from it; it is parallel to "I gave Zayd a dirham": Zayd is the agent [in meaning], because he is the taker of the dirham.

dervis-irab:39-41.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَوامِعُ): الصوامع is the plural of صومعة and صومع, which is a mountain or an elevated place that a monk or devotee inhabits seeking solitude; then the word was applied to the monastery. الصومعة is also the eagle, the hooded cloak (البرنس), and the top of any mountain if it is narrow-peaked.
(بِيَعٌ): the plural of بيعة, with kasra on the bāʾ: the place of worship of the Christians and the Jews; the plural is بيع, and بيعات with kasra on the bāʾ and fatḥa on the yāʾ, and بيعات with kasra on the bāʾ and sukūn on the yāʾ.
(وَصَلَواتٌ): with fatḥa on the ṣād and the lām, the plural of صلاة. The church was called صلاة because prayer is performed in it. It is also said to be an Arabicised word, its origin in Hebrew being صلوثا, with fatḥa on the ṣād and the thāʾ with three dots, as in al-Khafājī's (gloss) on al-Bayḍāwī. He said: and it was read thus among the anomalous (shādhdh) readings, and its meaning in their language is the place of prayer, so it is not figurative.

* I'rab:
(أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ): the sentence is resumptive, set out to grant permission to fight the polytheists. The believers used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, some beaten and some with head wounds, complaining, and he would say to them: "Be patient, for I have not been commanded to fight," until he emigrated; then this verse was revealed. It is the first verse in which permission to fight was given, after it had been forbidden in some seventy-odd verses.
أذن is a passive past verb, and the thing permitted is omitted because it is known, that is: permission to fight is given to those who are fought against. للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أذن; the clause يقاتلون is the ṣila (relative clause); يقاتلون is a passive imperfect, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). بأنهم is also attached to أذن, and the bāʾ is causal, that is, because of their being wronged; the clause ظلموا is the khabar (predicate) of أنهم. وإن الله على نصرهم لقدير: the wāw is resumptive, and the sentence is resumptive, set out to promise them victory by way of allusion and kināya (metonymy). إنّ with its noun, and قدير is its khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); على نصرهم is attached to قدير.
(الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَقُولُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ): الذين is a naʿt (adjective) or a badal (substitute) of the first relative noun; you may make it nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), to extol their worth and raise their standing. The clause أخرجوا is the ṣila, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; من ديارهم is attached to أخرجوا; بغير حق is a ḥāl (circumstantial). إلا is a particle of exception; أن يقولوا, the interpreted maṣdar, is a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ) in the position of accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī and others chose that the exception be "emptied" (mufarragh), because of the presence of negation through غير; so إلا is a particle of restriction, and أن يقولوا is in the position of genitive as a badal of حق, that is: without any cause except tawḥīd, which ought to be a cause for confirming them and establishing them, not a cause for expulsion and banishment. Its like is «هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ». ربنا is a mubtadaʾ and الله a khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as the speech-object of saying.
(وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَواتٌ وَمَساجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيراً): the wāw is resumptive; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence, containing the sense of condition. دفع الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is obligatorily omitted; الناس is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of دفع, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent, which is الله. The meaning is: were it not that Allah repels people by means of one another, the corrupters would prevail and the interests (of people) would be disrupted. Its opposite is rare in usage, namely that the maṣdar be annexed to its object and then its agent come in the nominative, as in the saying of al-Uqayshir al-Asadī:
أفنى تلادي وما جمعت من نشب ... قرع القواقيز أفواه الأباريق
(The knocking of the mouths of the ewers against the drinking-cups has consumed my inherited wealth and the property I gathered.)
قرع, with qāf and undotted ʿayn, is nominative as the agent of أفنى; it is a maṣdar annexed to its object, which is القواقيز — with two qāfs and a dotted zāy: cups from which wine is drunk; its singular is قاقوزة, with two dotted zāys [Translator's note: as written; قاقوزة has one zāy], so its plural is قوازيز [Translator's note: as written; the word in the verse is قواقيز]. أفواه is the agent of the maṣdar; it is the plural of فم, whose origin is فوه, and that is why (the hāʾ) is restored in the plural. However, the verse is also narrated with الأفواه in the accusative, in which case it is of the first kind.
بعضهم is a badal of part (badal baʿḍ) of الناس; ببعض is attached to دفع. The lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا; هدمت is a passive past verb; صوامع is the nāʾib fāʿil; بيع, صلوات and مساجد are conjoined to صوامع. The mention of the mosques was put last because hermitages, synagogues and churches are older in existence than they. The clause يذكر is a naʿt of the places mentioned; فيها is attached to يذكر; اسم الله is the nāʾib fāʿil; كثيرا is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, that is, much remembrance; or a naʿt of an omitted adverb, that is, much time.
(وَلَيَنْصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām prepares for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); ينصرن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis. الله is the agent; من is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause ينصره is the ṣila. The clause of إنّ and what follows it is an emphasis of the reason for the help: الله is its noun, the lām is the shifted lām, قوي is its first khabar and عزيز its second khabar.
(الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): الذين is a badal of the preceding الذين, or a second naʿt of the first الذين, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. You have another aspect, namely to parse it as a badal of «من ينصره»; al-Zajjāj mentioned this aspect; he said: that is, Allah will surely help those who, if We establish them… إن is conditional; مكناهم is a past verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi, and it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); في الأرض is attached to مكناهم; أقاموا is a past verb and agent, and it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); الصلاة is a mafʿūl bihi, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(وَلِلَّهِ عاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; لله is a fronted khabar, and عاقبة الأمور a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
Jihad is the peak of the hump of Islam:
The hadiths on jihad are many; we cite from them what rises to the peak of eloquence, following our method in this book. From Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Which deed is best?" He said: "Faith in Allah and His Messenger." It was said: "Then what?" He said: "Jihad in the path of Allah." It was said: "Then what?" He said: "An accepted (mabrūr) pilgrimage." Narrated by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Khuzayma in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
And from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with the people before the expedition of Tabūk. When morning came, he led the people in the dawn prayer; then the people mounted. When the sun rose, the people grew drowsy after the night journey, and Muʿādh kept close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, following in his track, while the people's mounts had scattered with them along the main roads, grazing and moving on. While Muʿādh was following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his she-camel was grazing at one time and moving on at another, Muʿādh's she-camel stumbled, so he jerked her jaw with the rein, and she sprang up so that the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shied from her. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ removed his head-covering and turned, and there was no one in the army nearer to him than Muʿādh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said: "O Muʿādh." He said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Come closer." So he drew near to us [Translator's note: as written; "to him" seems intended] until their two mounts were touching one another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I did not think the people were so far from us as they are." Muʿādh said: "O Prophet of Allah, the people grew drowsy, so their mounts scattered, grazing and moving on." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And I too was drowsy." When Muʿādh saw the cheerfulness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his being alone with him, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to ask you about a matter that has made me ill, made me sick and saddened me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask about whatever you wish." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise; I will not ask you about anything else." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bravo, bravo, bravo! You have asked about something tremendous" — three times — "and it is easy for one for whom Allah wills good; and it is easy for one for whom Allah wills good; and it is easy for one for whom Allah wills good." And he did not tell him anything without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeating it three times, out of eagerness that he should learn it well from him. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "You believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish the prayer, pay the zakāt, and worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him, until you die while you are upon that." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, repeat it for me," so he repeated it three times. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "If you wish, O Muʿādh, I will tell you of the head of this matter, the pillar of this matter, and the peak of the hump?" Muʿādh said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah; tell me, may my father and mother be your ransom." The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "The head of this matter is that you bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger; the pillar of this matter is establishing the prayer and paying the zakāt; and the peak of its hump is jihad in the path of Allah. I have only been commanded to fight people until they establish the prayer, pay the zakāt, and bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger; when they have done that, they have held fast and protected their blood and their property, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, no face has grown pale and no foot has become dusty in a deed by which the ranks of the Hereafter are sought, after the obligatory prayer, like jihad in the path of Allah; and nothing has made a servant's scale heavy like a mount spent in the path of Allah or ridden in the path of Allah."

dervis-irab:75-78.t:
* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا وَمِنَ النَّاسِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ) A resumptive clause brought to establish His, Exalted is He, choosing of the messengers. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (يصطفي) the khabar (predicate); (من الملائكة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of (رسلا) and was placed before it; you may also attach it to (يصطفي). (رسلا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من الناس) is conjoined to (من الملائكة), and [the object] is omitted from the second because the first indicates it, i.e. and He chooses messengers from among people. The clause (إن الله سميع بصير) gives the reason for what preceded, i.e. All-Hearing of what they say, All-Seeing of whom He takes as a messenger; (إن) and its noun; (سميع) is its first khabar and (بصير) its second khabar. (يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَما خَلْفَهُمْ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ) The clause (يعلم) is a third khabar, or resumptive. (يعلم) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; (ما) is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; (بين أيديهم): the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause); (وما خلفهم) is conjoined to (ما بين أيديهم). (وإلى الله): the wāw is a conjunction, and (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ترجع); (ترجع) is an imperfect passive verb and (الأمور) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ) The iʿrāb of (يا أيها الذين آمنوا) has been given before; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila. (اركعوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (اسجدوا) is conjoined to (اركعوا), and (اعبدوا ربكم) is also conjoined. (وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) (وافعلوا الخير) is conjoined to what preceded; the clause (لعلكم تفلحون) is a ḥāl of the wāw in (اركعوا) and what is conjoined to it, i.e. do these things while hoping for success. (وَجاهِدُوا فِي اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهادِهِ) (وجاهدوا) is also conjoined; (في الله) is attached to (جاهدوا), and there must be an omitted muḍāf, after the omission of the object of (جاهدوا), i.e. strive against your enemies for the sake of Allah and on His account; so (في) is causal. (حق جهاده) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(هُوَ اجْتَباكُمْ وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ) (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (اجتباكم), i.e. He chose you, is the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl of (الله). (وما): the wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative; (جعل) is a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "He"; (عليكم) is attached to an omitted second object of (جعل); (في الدين) is a ḥāl; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (حرج) is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is the first object of (جعل).
(مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْراهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَفِي هذا) There are several aspects for the accusative of (ملة), the most evident being what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned; his text is: «The milla is put in the accusative by the content of what precedes it, as if it were said: He has made your religion wide, with the widening of the milla of your father; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. It may also be put in the accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e. by the religion I specially mean the milla of your father»; or by an implied verb, its implied form being "follow". There are other aspects that do not go beyond these. (أبيكم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and (إبراهيم) is a badal (substitute) of (أبيكم). (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (سماكم) the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl of (إبراهيم); (سماكم) is a verb, a latent fāʿil and the first object, and (المسلمين) is the second object; (من قبل) is a ḥāl, i.e. before this Book, and (وفي هذا) is conjoined to (من قبل), i.e. and in this Qur'an.
(لِيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ شَهِيداً عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا شُهَداءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ) The lām is causal, and it is said it is of consequence (ʿāqiba); (يكون) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām; the lām and what it governs are attached to (سماكم). (الرسول) is the noun of (يكون) and (شهيدا) the khabar of (يكون); (عليكم) is attached to (شهيدا); (وتكونوا شهداء على الناس) is conjoined to its counterpart. (فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِاللَّهِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa); (أقيموا الصلاة) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and what follows is conjoined to it. (هُوَ مَوْلاكُمْ فَنِعْمَ الْمَوْلى وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ) The clause is a ḥāl of (الله); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (مولاكم) the khabar. (فنعم المولى): the fāʾ is resumptive; (نعم) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; (المولى) is the fāʿil, and the one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. "He"; (ونعم النصير) is conjoined to (نعم المولى).

dervis-irab:42-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِئْرٍ): in al-Mukhtār: "بأر بئرا, with a hamza after the bāʾ: he dug it; of the pattern قطع [Translator's note: printed as ربابه قطع; من باب قطع is evidently meant]." البئر is of the pattern فِعْل in the sense of مفعول, like الذبح in the sense of المذبوح: a large pit in the ground from which water is drawn; the plural is آبار, أبآر, بئار and أبؤر, and it is feminine. In al-Asās: "The great sinner is one who ابتأر, and the petty sinner one who ابتهر. One says: ابتأرت الجارية when he says 'I did it with her' and he is truthful, and ابتهرتها when he says that and he is lying. Al-Kumayt recited:
قبيح بمثلي نعت الفتا ... ة إما ابتهارا وإما ابتئارا
(It is ugly for one like me to describe a young woman, whether by lying boast or by true confession.)"
(مُعَطَّلَةٍ): abandoned through the death of its people, although it is in working order, with water in it and the tools for drawing water with it.
(مَشِيدٍ): raised high, plastered; from شاد البناء, that is, he raised it; one also says شيّد. In al-Nisāʾ it came from شيّد [Translator's note: as written; the reference is to مشيّدة in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:78], because there it occurred after a plural, whereas here it occurred after a singular, so the light form suited it.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَعادٌ وَثَمُودُ): the wāw is resumptive; the sentence is resumptive, set out to console the Prophet ﷺ, and (to show) that he is not unique in being given the lie. إن is conditional; يكذبوك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the wāw is the agent and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). فقد: the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is joined with قد; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); كذبت is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). قبلهم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبت; قوم نوح is the agent; عاد and ثمود are conjoined to قوم. قوم was treated as feminine with regard to the meaning of "nation" or "tribe". He did not say "the people of ʿĀd and Thamūd", dispensing with it because they are well known by these two names.
(وَقَوْمُ إِبْراهِيمَ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ): conjoined to what precedes.
(وَأَصْحابُ مَدْيَنَ وَكُذِّبَ مُوسى فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلْكافِرِينَ): وأصحاب مدين is conjoined. He turned away from "the people of Shuʿayb" because the people of Madyan were more deeply rooted in giving the lie than the people of the Thicket (al-Ayka); that is why He singled them out for mention. كذب is a passive past verb, and موسى is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). He varied the speech and did not say "the people of Mūsā", because, having opened the speech by recounting their giving the lie, then enumerated the kinds of those who gave the lie and their groups, and having reached Mūsā only after the speech had grown long, it was good to repeat it so that it would immediately precede His saying فأمليت, and so the effect would be joined to the cause — just as He said in the verse of (Sūrat) Qāf after enumerating them: «كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ», thus linking the punishment and the threat and joining them to the giving of the lie after renewing mention of it. فأمليت: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أمليت is a verb and agent; للكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمليت.
(ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval; أخذتهم is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi. فكيف: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; نكير is the noun of كان, that is, إنكاري (My disapproval), and the yāʾ was dropped. النكير is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of disapproval and changing (things), since He replaced their blessing with punishment, their life with destruction, and their building with ruin. The meaning of the interrogative will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها وَهِيَ ظالِمَةٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; the sentence is resumptive, set out to confirm what preceded by striking examples and citing evidence. كأين is predicative (khabariyya, "how many"), and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); من قرية is the tamyīz (specification) of كأين, and its verification has preceded. The clause أهلكناها, consisting of verb, agent and mafʿūl bihi, is the khabar of كأين. It is permissible for كأين to be accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by an omitted verb explained by أهلكناها, in which case the clause أهلكناها is explicative. وهي ظالمة: the wāw is circumstantial; هي is a mubtadaʾ and ظالمة a khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(فَهِيَ خاوِيَةٌ عَلى عُرُوشِها وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; هي is a mubtadaʾ and خاوية a khabar; the clause is conjoined to the clause أهلكناها. على عروشها is either attached to خاوية, in which case the meaning is that it has fallen down upon its roofs, that is, its roofs collapsed to the ground, then its walls were demolished and fell on top of the roofs; or it is a second khabar of هي, as though it were said: it is empty, and it is upon its roofs, that is, standing, overlooking its roofs, meaning that the roofs fell to the ground and came to be in line with the walls, and the walls remained standing, stark, looking down on the fallen roofs. Both estimations are beautiful and admissible. بئر is conjoined to قرية, that is, and how many a well; معطلة is a naʿt (adjective) of بئر; وقصر مشيد is also conjoined. Whether it is a specific well and a specific palace, or whether the two occur by way of a likeness — the discussion of all this will come in the Benefits section.
(أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ يَعْقِلُونَ بِها أَوْ آذانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِها): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī) if they had travelled, or for urging travel so that they may see the places where those before them fell. The fāʾ conjoins to an implied element required by the context, that is: did they neglect and disregard, and travel and not benefit? لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past meaning) and jussivisation; يسيروا is an imperfect verb made jussive by لم, and the wāw is its agent; في الأرض is attached to يسيروا. فتكون: the fāʾ is causal, and تكون is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the causal fāʾ; لهم is the fronted khabar of تكون, and قلوب its postponed noun; the clause يعقلون is a naʿt of قلوب, and بها is attached to يعقلون. أو is a conjunction, and آذان is conjoined to قلوب; the clause يسمعون بها is a naʿt of آذان. It is clear that what is derived from the negated also entails negation.
(فَإِنَّها لا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصارُ وَلكِنْ تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ): the fāʾ is for causation; إنّ with its noun, the pronoun referring to the story or the matter (al-qiṣṣa aw al-shaʾn); the clause لا تعمى الأبصار is the khabar. ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), made inoperative because it is lightened; تعمى القلوب is an imperfect verb and agent; التي is a naʿt of القلوب; في الصدور is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The secret of His saying في الصدور will come in the Rhetoric section.

* Rhetoric:
1- The interrogative in the saying of the Exalted «فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ» means affirmation (taqrīr), which is leading the addressee to acknowledge what he knows but disputes, resorting to obstinacy and sophistry in opposing it. Abū Ḥayyān said: "This interrogative is accompanied by the sense of wonder, as though it were said: how severe was My disapproval of them!" And this too is clear; so the interrogative is, then, for affirmation with wonder.
2- Infiṣāl (anticipating and resolving an objection) in the saying of the Exalted «وَلكِنْ تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ». For someone might say: hearts are only ever in the breasts, so what benefit is there in mentioning what is familiar and existent, since it is known? The resolution of that is to say: what is familiar is that real blindness has its place in the eyesight, because it is the affliction of the pupil with what effaces its light, and its use for the heart is figurative (majāz). So when it was intended to transfer it from the literal to the figurative, the speech amounted to affirming what is contrary to the familiar and to the original, so it needed additional specification, so that it would be established that blindness has its place in the hearts, not in the eyes. It is as when you say: "Sharpness does not belong to the sword, but to your tongue which is between your jaws": your saying "between your jaws" establishes what you have claimed for his tongue and the denial of sharpness of the sword, which is the familiar. This is among the rare gems of eloquence, so understand it. The upshot of the matter is that the defect is not in their senses, for they are sound with no fault in them; rather the defect is in their relapsed intellects and their disabled minds.

* Benefits:
The abandoned well and the lofty palace: it is said that they are specific. Al-Khaṭīb al-Shirbīnī said in his tafsīr: "It is narrated that this well is the one at which Ṣāliḥ alighted with four thousand persons of those who believed in him, and Allah the Exalted saved them from the punishment; it is in Ḥaḍramawt, and it was so called only because Ṣāliḥ was present (حضر) at it when he died. And there, at the well [Translator's note: printed as عبد البئر; عند البئر seems intended], is a town named Ḥāḍūrā, which the people of Ṣāliḥ built; they appointed over themselves Julhus ibn Julās and dwelt there for a time; then they disbelieved and worshipped an idol, and Allah sent to them Ḥanẓala ibn Ṣafwān as a prophet, but they killed him, so Allah the Exalted destroyed them, abandoned their well and ruined their palaces." The preferable view is that the well is general and the palace is general, that is: how many a town We have destroyed, how many a well We have left idle, without those who draw from it, and how many a lofty palace whose people have dispersed from it and whose inhabitants have moved away from it.

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَرِيدٍ): insolent, stripped bare for corruption. al-Zajjāj said: al-marīd and al-mārid is the one who is high and smooth. And it is said in al-Qāmūs and its commentary: al-mārid is the insolent, the lofty; one says "a mārid building", i.e. a lofty one, and this is figurative (majāz); its plural is maradah, māridūn and murrād. And al-marīd is the one intense in defiance, the vile and wicked; its plural is murd and its feminine is mardāʾ. One says: "murd on jurd", i.e. beardless youths on short-haired horses.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌ) يا is a particle of vocative; أَيُّهَا is an indefinite, specified vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for alerting; النَّاسُ is a badal (substitute) for أَيُّ in wording; اتَّقُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ: إنّ and its noun; شَيْءٌ is its khabar and عَظِيمٌ an adjective of شَيْءٌ; the clause إنّ زلزلة الساعة etc. is causal and has no grammatical position, owing to His saying اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ. And زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ is the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent or to its object. On the first, it is as though the Hour itself were what shakes things, by figurative attribution (majāz ḥukmī); on the second, it follows the way of extension in the adverbial, treating it as a direct object, like His saying «بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ». (يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَها تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَها)
The adverbial is attached to تَذْهَلُ, and the clause تَرَوْنَها is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverbial. They allowed other possibilities for it, among them that it be attached to عَظِيمٌ, or to an implied اذْكُرْ ("remember"), or that it be a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) of زَلْزَلَةَ, since each of the event and the time can be said to include the other. The pronoun in تَرَوْنَها refers to the Hour, i.e. the Resurrection, since it is of such a degree as to cut the vessels of the hearts; it may also refer to the earthquake (zalzala), and perhaps this is nearer since it is in this world. تَذْهَلُ is a nominative imperfect verb; كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ is the agent; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of تَرَوْنَها, i.e. the hāʾ — for the seeing here is certainly by sight. This holds if we do not make يَوْمَ attached to تَذْهَلُ; if it is attached to it, the ḥāl is not allowed and the clause becomes resumptive, or else it is a ḥāl from the earthquake, or from the latent pronoun in عَظِيمٌ, or from the Hour even though it is a muḍāf ilayhi, because it is either an agent or a direct object, as stated above. In that case an omitted pronoun must be implied, i.e. "she is distracted in it". The murḍiʿa (with tāʾ marbūṭa) is the one actually engaged in nursing, having put her breast in the infant's mouth, whereas the murḍiʿ (without it) is the one whose nature it is to nurse, whether she is actually nursing or not; so they distinguished between the two with the tāʾ marbūṭa. More detail on this secret will come in the chapter on rhetoric. عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ is attached to تَذْهَلُ, and ما is a relative or a maṣdar particle, i.e. "from that which she nursed" or "from her nursing". وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ: an imperfect verb and an agent, and the clause is conjoined to the clause تَذْهَلُ; ذاتِ حَمْلٍ is a muḍāf to كُلُّ and حَمْلَها is the direct object of تَضَعُ. al-ḥamL with fatḥa on the unpointed ḥāʾ is what is in the belly or on a tree, and with kasra it is what is on the back. (وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ)
The wāw is a conjunction; تَرَى is an imperfect verb conjoined to تَرَوْنَها. It is plural in the first and singular in the second only because the first seeing is tied to the earthquake or the Hour, which all people see, whereas the second is tied to people being drunk, so each person must be made a seer of the rest, disregarding his own being described as drunk. The agent of تَرَى is latent, its implied form being "you"; النَّاسَ is a direct object; سُكارى is a ḥāl; the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; ما is a negative in the Ḥijāzī manner; هُمْ is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and سُكارى is genitive in wording and accusative in position as the khabar of ما; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from النَّاسَ. Both ḍamma and fatḥa are possible on the sīn of سُكارى — they are two dialects, and it has been read with both. As for وَلكِنَّ, the wāw is a conjunction on an omitted element, contrasting with what follows لكنّ, and this is a regular ruling for it. The implied form, as in al-Baḥr of Abū Ḥayyān: «These states — the distraction, the delivering, and seeing people like the drunk — are mild and gentle, but the punishment of Allah is severe, i.e. not gentle and not easy; so what follows لكنّ contrasts with what precedes it.» More discussion of this verse will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to mention the one who was heedless of the recompense in that and denied it; the connection between it and what precedes of the mention of the terrors of the Hour and its earthquake is plain. مِنَ النَّاسِ is a fronted khabar; مَنْ is certainly an indefinite described noun, and it is a delayed mubtadaʾ, i.e. people described by disputation, obstinacy, sophistry and stubborn arrogance, among whom admonitions are of no use and proofs have no effect. The clause يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ is an adjective of مَنْ, and the pronoun is singular in regard to the wording of مَنْ; had it been plural in regard to its meaning, it would have been permissible. فِي اللَّهِ is attached to يُجادِلُ, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "His power, His attributes and His religion". بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ is a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in يُجادِلُ, i.e. ignorant, stumbling in the wildernesses of blind misguidance and abominable ignorance. (وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ مَرِيدٍ) وَيَتَّبِعُ is conjoined to يُجادِلُ; كُلَّ is a direct object; شَيْطانٍ is a muḍāf ilayhi; and مَرِيدٍ
is an adjective of شَيْطانٍ; an omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "the footsteps of every devil". (كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ) كُتِبَ is a passive past verb; عَلَيْهِ is attached to it; أنّ and what is within its scope is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; مَنْ is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ — it is also possible that مَنْ be a relative noun and a mubtadaʾ with فَأَنَّهُ as the khabar, the fāʾ having entered because of the scent of condition in the relative; the clause يُضِلُّهُ is the khabar of أنّه, and the clause of the condition or the relative is the khabar of أنّه. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that فَأَنَّهُ be conjoined to the first, and Abū Ḥayyān took him to task, saying: this is not allowed, because if you make فَأَنَّهُ conjoined to أنّه, then أنّه is left without a complete khabar. Yet many have supported al-Zamakhsharī in his i'rab, and we see that what we have chosen is nearer to the correct. وَيَهْدِيهِ is conjoined to يُضِلُّهُ, and إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ is attached to يَهْدِيهِ.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى»
is a tashbīh baligh (eloquent simile), for He likened the people on that harsh day to the state of the drunk, who have lost discrimination and squandered right guidance. The scholars say: among the proofs of figurative speech is that its contrary can truthfully be said, as in your saying "Zayd is a donkey" when you describe him as dull and stupid, and then it is true to say "he is not a donkey", denying him the literal sense. Likewise the verse, after affirming figurative drunkenness, denied the literal sense with the most emphatic denial, strengthened by the bāʾ. The secret of its emphasis is to alert that this drunkenness that is upon them in that state is nothing of the familiar kind, but is a matter they had never known the like of before. And the rectification (istidrāk) by His saying «وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ»
returns to His saying وما هم بسكارى, and it is as though it were an explanation for affirming the figurative drunkenness, as if it were said: If they are not drunk from wine, which is the familiar drunkenness, what then is this strange drunkenness, and what is its cause? So it was said: the severity of the punishment of Allah the Exalted.
2- In His turning from murḍiʿ to murḍiʿa there is a secret few perceive. It is that the murḍiʿa is the one who has actually been nursing, so her pulling her breast from her child's mouth when the terror occurs is more indicative of bewilderment, and a fuller embodiment of the places of distraction that overcame her. There is another difference: the form that comes by attribution (nasab), i.e. murḍiʿ, takes no account of the occurrence of the attribute from which it is derived, but implies that its subject is described by it; whereas the form not by attribution, i.e. murḍiʿa, takes account of the occurrence of the act and the attribute's issuing from it. And this is among the secrets of our language that are rare in other languages.
And it is said in al-Mufaṣṣal: «The doctrine of the Kufans is that the tāʾ is omitted from ḥāʾiḍ because it is dispensed with, and this requires the tāʾ to be kept where there is ambiguity, as in ḍāmir, ʿāshiq, ayyim, thayyib and ʿānis.» This objection is clear. As for the objection from the retention of the tāʾ in attributes specific to females, such as imraʾa maʿība and kalba mujriya according to al-Ṣiḥāḥ, it is not sound, because what they mentioned is permitted, not required, for they say that bringing the tāʾ where it can be dispensed with is the original, like ḥāmila for the woman. It is said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: One says imraʾa ḥāmil and ḥāmila when she is pregnant; whoever says ḥāmil says this is an adjective, and whoever says ḥāmila builds it on "ḥamalat, so she is ḥāmila". And he recited a verse of ʿAmr ibn Ḥassān:
تمخضت المنون له بيوم ... أتى ولكل حاملة تمام
(Fate was in labour for him with a day that came; and every pregnant one has her term.)
But if she carries something on her back or on her head, she is ḥāmila and nothing else.
